Just Cause 4 – Bigger, Bolder, but Not Quite Better
Rating: 8/10

Just Cause 4 builds on the explosive sandbox foundation of its predecessor but stumbles slightly in the execution. While it introduces impressive new weather systems and visual upgrades, it loses some of the charm and chaos that made Just Cause 3 a fan favorite.

Visuals & World – 9/10
The fictional country of Solís is visually stunning, featuring diverse biomes like jungles, deserts, and snow-covered peaks. Dynamic weather effects — including tornadoes and lightning storms — are genuinely impressive and add spectacle to the mayhem. Technically, it’s a leap forward from JC3, with sharper visuals and more environmental variety.

Gameplay – 8/10
Rico still has his grappling hook, parachute, and wingsuit, but now with customizable mods that allow for more creative chaos. However, the destruction feels less satisfying, and the mission structure becomes repetitive. The emphasis on faction-based territory control doesn’t fully land, often breaking the game’s pacing.

Story – 6.5/10
The plot tries to go deeper into Rico’s past and the mysterious weather tech, but it’s largely forgettable. Characters lack depth, and the writing doesn’t carry the self-aware energy of earlier entries.

Sound & Polish – 7.5/10
The sound design is solid, especially during weather events, but the game launched with noticeable bugs and AI issues (many later patched). The overall experience feels less refined compared to the more cohesive fun of Just Cause 3.

Verdict:
Just Cause 4 is a visually superior game with ambitious ideas — especially the extreme weather mechanics — but it doesn’t recapture the pure, explosive joy of Just Cause 3. It's still a fun sandbox if you’re in the mood for destruction, but it feels like a step sideways rather than forward.

This game delivers exactly what you’d expect: non-stop explosions, ridiculous stunts, and pure joy in blowing absolutely everything to pieces. The vehicles? A wild mix of Mad Max and toy cars loaded with dynamite - delightfully stupid in the best way. The grappling hook with physics mods turns the world into your personal destruction playground.

Unfortunately, the game tries a bit too hard to be serious. The story takes up way too much space and isn't nearly as compelling as it thinks it is (and you can't skip the cutscenes). Instead of embracing the chaos, you keep getting dragged into a convoluted plot about rebels and weather machines. And don’t get me started on the squad system - clunky, unnecessary, and completely at odds with the game’s anarchic spirit.

Just Cause is at its best when it forgets to be serious. If you’re into explosive mayhem, crazy stunts, and total freedom to be a one-man wrecking crew, this is your game. Just ignore the plot and the annoying squad mechanics, and enjoy the ride. It's like Far Cry on a sugar rush: loud, dumb, and a whole lot of fun.

I think on launch this game was kinda lacking, even messy. I remember it being buggy way back then, and just not as fun or endearing as Just Cause 3. However, I think now it's pretty fun, and the DLCs are really cool. They add a lot of fun things to do to the game, along with the other things which make it enjoyable. I like that the missions are set up differently based on where you are. In Just Cause 3, every outpost was just blow up everything until it's at 0%, which I did enjoy, however it is a very repetitive loop. I also like the diversity in biomes you can explore. It makes the map feel almost continental in scale. There are a few immersion issues in the story. For instance, every voice actor sounds like a hispanic person from Los Angeles, not really like South Americans. The setting is supposed to be a place with its own dialect of spanish, but they don't commit to making that happen. Also the Black Hand as an enemy are OK if unrealistic. This regime controls a massive amount of land including many large cities, and doesn't have a police force? It's just the army everywhere? Not even army npcs with police cars. JC3 did this better I think. One thing I love totally is the frontline battles which you can actually manipulate and take part in. I think that is something every game going forward should have. In the far distant future when we get JC5 I hope it is an improvement on this game, with a unique map, unique and deep mechanics, a compelling story, and a fun gameplay loop. Maybe they could set the next one in the Middle East, Eastern Europe, or a North-Korea type place? I think those would be great settings

[h1] Just Cause 4 - Unleashing the Chaos in a Bigger Playground[/h1]

Graphics: ★★★★☆
Just Cause 4 continues the series tradition of delivering a visually impressive open-world playground. The South American-inspired setting introduces diverse landscapes, from lush rainforests to arid deserts. Improved weather effects, especially the dynamic and dramatic storms, add a layer of realism and spectacle. However, occasional graphical glitches and pop-in issues can momentarily disrupt the experience.

Gameplay: ★★★★☆
Building upon the foundation laid by its predecessor, Just Cause 4 refines the formula with enhanced grappling hook mechanics and an expanded set of tools for creative destruction. The addition of extreme weather events, including tornadoes and lightning storms, introduces new dimensions to chaos. While the core gameplay remains enjoyable, some may find that the incremental improvements don't revolutionize the experience.

Story: ★★★☆☆
Just Cause 4, like its predecessors, prioritizes action over a deep narrative. The plot serves as a backdrop for the chaos, and while it provides context for Rico Rodriguez's missions, it may not leave a lasting impression. The characters and storyline are serviceable, but the focus remains on the player's ability to unleash havoc across the vast landscapes.

Soundtrack: ★★★☆☆
The soundtrack complements the game's high-energy action with a mix of dynamic tunes. However, the music may not be particularly memorable outside of intense gameplay moments. The sound effects shine, especially during chaotic encounters and explosive setpieces, adding to the overall sensory experience.

Level Design: ★★★☆☆
Just Cause 4 features a massive and diverse world, showcasing different regions with unique challenges. The improved weather system contributes to dynamic gameplay scenarios, and the variety in landscapes keeps exploration interesting. However, the lack of significant improvements in settlement design and the occasional repetition in objectives may feel familiar to series veterans.

Replayability: ★★★★☆
The sandbox nature of Just Cause 4 offers ample replay value. Liberation of regions, completion of challenges, and experimenting with the extensive array of weapons and vehicles provide plenty of reasons to return. The addition of extreme weather events introduces new possibilities for creative chaos and adds to the game's longevity.

Overall: ★★★★☆
Just Cause 4 builds upon the series' chaotic foundation, offering a larger playground for destruction and mayhem. While it may not represent a revolutionary leap forward, the refinements in gameplay mechanics and the introduction of dynamic weather events keep the experience fresh and enjoyable. For fans of the series and those who relish open-world chaos, Just Cause 4 provides a thrilling, albeit familiar, adventure in explosive liberation.

Just Cause 4 is an explosive open-world action game that delivers on the franchise’s promise of chaotic fun and over-the-top stunts, though it arrives with a mixed bag of improvements and noticeable flaws. Developed by Avalanche Studios, the game thrusts players into the vibrant, yet dangerous world of Solis, a fictional South American country beset by extreme weather, political turmoil, and a powerful private militia known as the Black Hand. As Rico Rodriguez, the iconic protagonist, players are tasked with dismantling the regime of an oppressive villain while navigating massive landscapes filled with opportunities for destruction and mayhem.

One of Just Cause 4’s most impressive features is its dynamic weather system, which introduces tornadoes, thunderstorms, and sandstorms that drastically affect gameplay and add a layer of unpredictability to the already chaotic combat scenarios. These natural disasters not only provide visually stunning moments but also influence tactics — tornadoes can throw vehicles and enemies into the air, while lightning storms might cause explosive chain reactions. This weather mechanic enriches the open-world experience, making exploration feel fresh and challenging. The map itself is vast and diverse, ranging from dense jungles and snowy peaks to arid deserts and sprawling urban areas, each offering unique environmental hazards and mission types.

Gameplay remains true to the series’ DNA, focusing on fast-paced, destructive action combined with Rico’s signature grapple hook, parachute, and wingsuit. These traversal tools enable incredible freedom of movement, allowing players to chain together jaw-dropping stunts and creative takedowns. The combat is highly customizable thanks to the ability to upgrade weapons, gadgets, and vehicles, encouraging experimentation with different playstyles. Missions often revolve around sabotage, base assaults, and high-speed chases, all designed to maximize player creativity and destruction. However, despite the freedom, some missions feel repetitive, relying heavily on similar objectives that can dampen the overall momentum after extended play.

Graphically, Just Cause 4 offers beautiful vistas and detailed environments, though it occasionally suffers from technical issues such as pop-in textures, frame rate drops, and clipping. The weather effects are particularly well-executed, showcasing the game’s ambition in visual design. Audio design complements the chaos, with explosive sound effects, an energetic soundtrack, and solid voice acting that bring the world of Solis to life. While the story itself is relatively straightforward and sometimes predictable, it provides enough motivation to push through the campaign and engage with the world.

Despite its strengths, Just Cause 4 has drawn criticism for a number of bugs and glitches present at launch, some of which persist, impacting immersion and gameplay smoothness. The AI can also feel inconsistent — enemy behavior ranges from overly aggressive to strangely passive, reducing tactical challenge in certain encounters. Additionally, the multiplayer absence and lack of significant innovation compared to previous entries leave some players wanting more. Nevertheless, the core experience of chaos, destruction, and freedom remains intact, and for fans of the franchise, these shortcomings are often outweighed by the sheer fun of wreaking havoc in an open world.

In conclusion, Just Cause 4 is a thrilling, if somewhat flawed, open-world action game that delivers spectacular weather effects, expansive environments, and the trademark explosive gameplay that the series is known for. While it struggles with repetitive mission design, occasional technical hiccups, and AI quirks, its core mechanics and the freedom it offers players make it a compelling experience for those who enjoy large-scale, sandbox destruction. For newcomers and longtime fans alike, Just Cause 4 offers a wild ride full of action and adventure, even if it doesn’t quite reach the heights of its predecessors.

From grappling across stunning landscapes to unleashing explosive destruction, Rico Rodriguez's latest adventure is a wild journey that will keep you on the edge of your seat. However, it's important to acknowledge a couple of drawbacks that might give some players pause.

Let's start with the positives. The vast South American open-world setting is a visual spectacle, offering a diverse and expansive playground for players to explore. The dynamic weather system and day-night cycles add a level of realism that enhances the overall immersion. Rico's signature grappling hook and wingsuit are back, and the improvements to these mechanics make traversing the vast landscapes a joy, allowing for creative approaches to missions and adding an extra layer of excitement.

The storyline is engaging, filled with unexpected twists and turns, and the characters are well-crafted, adding depth to the narrative. The voice acting is commendable, bringing the characters to life and making the story more compelling.

While these instances aren't game-breaking, they can be frustrating and momentarily disrupt the otherwise seamless flow of the action. It's worth noting that developers have been actively working on patches to address these concerns, so it's possible that future updates may improve the overall stability.

On the visual front, Just Cause 4 falls a bit short of expectations. While the open-world environments are stunning, the graphics can be somewhat inconsistent, with moments of brilliance punctuated by occasional mediocrity. Some textures may lack the polish seen in other contemporary titles, and the visual fidelity doesn't consistently match the grandiosity of the game's scale.

In conclusion, Just Cause 4 is a thrilling experience for fans of explosive open-world action. Despite a few hiccups such as occasional game freezes and inconsistencies in graphics, the sheer fun and excitement of the gameplay make it a worthwhile adventure. Its an alright game, but it removes a lot of features from JC3, such as the explosives and dual wielding pistols. The enemy AI is also much less forgiving, with helicopters appearing with only one level of Heat.

This is a hard one to recommend... as it's the worst in the series... and it's so repetitive with only a limited number of mission types, it's a lot of rinse and repeat stuff. The physics engine is a little broken, though sometimes in a good way. The cutscenes are laughably poorly made and way too compressed for anything made in the last 15-20 years. But once you get passed that, it has it's moments, but it can't hold a candle to the 2nd or even 3rd games. Feels like they might have spent way too much time making it multiplayer and not enough time making the single player experience less frustrating.

But hey, even if it's the weak link, the series had a strong start and it's difficult to bring your A game every time. If you're into the series, you might find enough to keep you entertained for a few hours. Certainly a one and done for me.

TL;DR
- Does JC4 deserve all the hate comments you've read right here? Nope; game runs fine and the story's not better nor worse than the other JC episodes
- Is JC3 better than JC4? Yep. JC4 tried to change stuff but JC3 feels better overall.
- Is JC4 _fun to play_? Certainly!

The Good
- Everything that makes Just Cause fun is there : grappling action, lots of vehicles to drive, crazy chases with the local militia, blowing stuff up... you name it!
- Conquering an area doesn't require you to spend ages looking for the very last transformer to blow up anymore \o/
- The JC4 soundtrack is the best of the series

The Bad
- Extreme weather (of of JC4's major selling points) is limited to a few scripted areas
- Not as much variety in vehicles / vehicle colours as in JC3
- Vehicle collecting mechanism has become ridiculous : "find Waldo and cross the ring" vs. JC3's "bring it to the garage in one piece" which was tons of fun

The Ugly
- Incomprehensible heat level meter
- Enemies may pop up out of nowhere to keep the pressure on, to the point of nonsense

All in all, game's worth $15 imo. Go for it if you've finished and appreciated JC3. If not, play JC3 first  =D

Ok... So... Just Cause 4... Just Cause 4 Reloaded is... absolutely fine. That's it, fine. Not awful, not bad, not horrendous like some people say, it's just fine. When compared to JC2 or JC3, yeah, not good looks, but looking at it as it's own game, it's fine, even great at some fronts.

Just Cause 4 finally has a different story than "overthrow an authoritarian regime in Central America", also, finally some character development too, Rico is a bit more grumpy than expected, but still a good character. The story has... Something! They tried for once, it's no God of War but it gets the job done, and of course, ends on a cliffhanger. I will never forgive you if you don't give us a JC5 Avalanche >:(

Gameplay is better in every way imaginable (M/KB), some things were added, some removed, some changed (don't know who had the idea to auto-retract the tethers >.>), but overall, I still like it. Much easier to control Rico in the wingsuit and use all the gadgets. 
Gunfight is still the same as JC2 and JC3, and by that I mean that it still awful. Using the rifles feels like you are shooting stone statues with a healthbar and that's it. No impact animations, no blood wounds, no physics, no gore, once their health reaches zero, the stiff statues become a ragdoll, and that's it. 
Use explosive weapons or shotguns, believe me, much better.

Action is still awesome, destruction physics are the best of all JC games, the tornadoes ripping through the land and taking everything along with it is marvelous, I do wish we had more control of the weather effects tho, it's pretty complicated to control the Tornadoes for example. Ah yes, the turret sections are fun too.

The mission structure is... Strange, you have to release a few regions to unlock main missions, it's fine tho, can get tiresome but nothing extreme. I just played the main campaign, wasn't in the mood to 100% the game, I just released the regions and made the main missions, had a pretty decent time, but if you do all sides it will probably take forever and be boring.

Graphics are a mixed bag, the horizons looks beautiful, the explosion effects are among the best I have ever seen, the particles, fire, rain effects, all brilliant. As for the atmosphere, it has a darker tone to it, specially when compared to JC3, it's taste, I like it but I get those who enjoy a more vibrant experience. As for the bad, man, the lightning and texture work of the cutscenes are HORRENDOUS, my god, what happened there? Literal PS1 textures, sometimes the hair glitches, Sheldon looked like he had metal hair and beard on some cutscenes, the cutscenes are waaaay too dark and low res (literally 480p), I don't know why they did it, the in-game cutscenes are MUCH better. Last, of course, the ocean, yea the water is strange man, while it looks good at night with winds, during the day it looks like paper. Awful.

The performance is also fine for me, no framedrops at all, not even in tornadoes, the FPS is completely stable, much better performance than JC3 in all possible fronts and I had a single crash while playing and reproducing a stream on my second monitor. The only stutters I had was when I completed a leaderboard challenge, but once I disabled those in the menu, no more stutters.

As an old time fan that played all JC games (Really old, JC1 on PS2 was fire), I actually like it. Not the best Just Cause, but not the atrocity people make it. 
I would give it mixed rating, but since I like it more than dislike it. Soft recommended.

Just Cause 4 is an action-packed open-world game developed by Avalanche Studios. Set in the fictional South American country of Solis, the game follows the adventures of Rico Rodriguez, a mercenary known for his ability to cause chaos and destruction. The gameplay is thrilling, offering players an immense amount of freedom to explore and wreak havoc with a variety of tools, from guns and explosives to a grappling hook and wingsuit. The open world is vast and diverse, with different environments ranging from jungles to deserts, mountains. However, while the game excels in terms of fun, there are still a few downsides. The storyline, while competent, feels a bit formulaic, and the dialogue lacks depth at times. The AI can also be a bit repetitive, with enemies often acting in predictable ways. That said, Just Cause 4 is still a blast for those who love mindless fun, destruction, and open-world exploration. If you don’t mind the lack of narrative depth and the occasional repetitive gameplay, it’s a great choice for fans of the franchise.

Just Cause 4 – гэта экшн-гра ў адкрытым свеце, распрацаваная студыяй Avalanche. Дзеянне гульні разгортваецца ў вымышленай паўднёваамерыканскай краіне Соліс, дзе галоўны герой Рыка Родрыгес, наёмнік, вядомы сваёй здольнасцю выклікаць хаос і разбурэнні.  Гульня прапануе вялікую свабоду дзеянняў, даючы магчымасць даследаваць велізарны свет і весці знішчэнне з дапамогай розных інструментаў, такіх як агнястрэльная зброя, выбухоўкі, а таксама каўза (граплінг) і крылаты касцюм. Свет гульні шырокі і разнастайны, з джунглямі, пустынямі, гарамі. Тым не менш, нягледзячы на тое, што гульня забяспечвае шмат забавы, ёсць некалькі недахопаў. Сюжэт, хаця і прыстойны, здаецца трохі шаблонным, а дыялогі часам не маюць глыбіні. Штучны інтэлект таксама можа быць досыць паўтаральным, бо ворагі часта дзейнічаюць прадказальна. Тым не менш, Just Cause 4 застанецца выдатным выбарам для тых, хто любіць разбурэнне і адкрытыя светлыя прыгоды. Калі вам не важна паглыбленне ў сюжэт і часам паўтаральнасць гульнявога працэсу, гэта выдатны выбар для фанатаў франшызы.

Just Cause 4 – це захоплююча екшн-гра в відкритому світі, розроблена студією Avalanche. Події гри відбуваються в вигаданій південноамериканській країні Соліс, де головний герой, найманець Ріко Родрігес, відомий своєю здатністю створювати хаос і руйнувати все навколо. Ігровий процес вражає. Гравцям надається велика свобода для дослідження величезного світу і можливість розгромити все, що попадається під руку, використовуючи різноманітні інструменти – від зброї та вибухівки до гачка і крилатого костюма. Світ гри різноманітний: від джунглів і пустель до гір. Проте, незважаючи на розважальність гри, є й кілька недоліків. Сюжет хоч і достатньо цікавий, але здається дещо стандартним, а діалоги інколи не мають глибини. Штучний інтелект інколи здається повторюваним, оскільки вороги часто діють передбачувано. Проте, Just Cause 4 – це чудовий вибір для тих, хто любить руйнацію, відкриті світи та пригоди. Якщо вам не критичні сюжетні глибини і іноді повторюваний ігровий процес, то ця гра – чудовий варіант для фанатів серії.

What an unfortunate end to the series... This year I've decided to get through all four games for the first time and, to be quite honest, I don't think that this game is as bad as the fan-base thinks. Well, yeah, it's pretty buggy (sometimes not even in a fun way) and a downfall from JC3, but I don't think it's bad on it's own. The main problem is because the formula has already been done and the developers didn't know what to do anymore. The missions are mostly "do those 3 things" or "protect this guy", which to me was not all that tedious, as I personally prefer linearity in open-world games. The tower defense missions were annoying though. The game tries to go more with JC2 structure in progression, where we have this number of minor missions to complete before a cool big mission. I feel like this game succeeded in that, not better than JC2 though to be honest. The art-style and graphics, while not that pretty like in JC3, I think look quite good. I actually like how big the country feels here. The story was never a strong suit for the series and they tried to make it serious this time, which actually made me pretty interested. Unfortunately the characters themselves while not bad, are also nothing special. They and Rico just support each other and that's what you're going to hear throughout the game, not much connection besides that. The soundtrack is good by the way, almost to the JC1 quality.

What I didn't enjoy is the new adjustments. There are a lot of new ways you can use your grappling hook and they are mostly useless. There are no grenades this time around, instead each weapon has it's own explosive. Requires time to get used to. For some reason there are now multiple pilots you can fast-travel with, which doesn't make sense why would they even add that? The main villain, or villains for that matter, are not that interesting. And even the final fight was just an enemy rush, which was highly disappointing, considering this was the person Rico personally wanted to get rid of. I guess I enjoyed the moments where you're gliding towards a tornado, but that's mostly just looks and don't impact you gameplay-wise. The side-missions are pretty generic most of the time. The main point of JC2 or JC3, which was causing destruction - took a backseat, which is a weird decision, to say the least.

Overall, the game is not bad. Just a disappointment, nothing else. You can just see that the developers didn't know what to do here. And that's a shame. Is it worth playing? Well, if you enjoyed JC2 more than JC3, maybe. That can also be an okay way for a first acquaintance with the series, but we all know that everybody will jump to JC3 right away. I had a good time here, maybe you'll have too. Just Cause is always dirt cheap on sale anyway, so I don't think it will be a waste to try this one. But for a last game in a series, that's a shame how this is how things ended.

At the time of writing this review, I have just 100% Just Cause 3. And intend the same for JC4. So, I’ll be revisiting this review as I complete the game. Now, please remember I’m coming into this game assuming its mechanics are similar to JC3.

First 5 hours:
My initial response reflects my previous review, negative… The game feels off, with mechanics that feel clunky. For example, movement. While I expected there to be some changes, I didn't expect to change most of my keybinds. On top of that, ground movement feels delayed. Rico, my sweet boy, tends to forget about running. I’ll try to walk forward, and my man here is lost to the wind. While I’ve gotten used to this, it lowkey pissed me off for the 1st hour. Another pet peeve of mine is the auto retractor. It bugged me early on, but I’ve gotten used to it. Another issue I’m having with JC4 is the UI. JC3 was clean, easy to understand, bright, and interesting. But they’ve ripped up the previous mechanics. On your map, it’s become a lot harder to see bases and places you’ve been. The map is also much darker, and while I don't mind me some dark mode. When I get flashbanged every time I exit the map, it sorta sucks. Traveling to the next tab, you’ll find what's replaced the gears tab. Your grappling hook upgrades. It's a less interesting, more boring waste of space. Moving on with our UI tour, the “supply drop” (replacing the previous rebel drop) isn't half bad. I don't entirely mind it, I just miss the ability to drop 1 car and 3 weapons. Now it's one at a time :/ But it's not too big a problem when Rico, God bless this man. He throws his gun, the second its empty… In JC3, when you ran out of ammo, he kept his gun, letting you get more ammo. But na, this man is praying on my downfall. Now thankfully I’m a pro gamer, and get a new gun. But I’ve found myself without guns a few times, and that's extremely annoying when the black hand is constantly on your ass. It’s very hard to tell how much heat you have and how close you are to losing it. On top of that, it doesn't help when it feels like you're heat 4, 24/7! I appreciate them showing some love for the vehicles, letting them get used by the AI. But god dam bro. Cut me some slack! Now venting aside, a few thing I am enjoying about this game is the map. It’s pretty beautiful, and knowing if you can see it, you can go there makes it a lot cooler. Another thing I like is that if you’ve purchased the “Toy Vehicle Pack“, when you hop in one, the black hand will also pull out their reserve of tiny vehicles. So, summary? Ya, I’d get this game. Just need some time to adjust. Hopefully, my next update is all positive! :)

18 hours in:
So, my next update is Positive! While it failed to meet the bar set by JC3, it’s only slightly under par, and is still a fun game. So to start of with, I’m really starting to miss those 3 gun slots. I liked carrying a rifle, sniper, and special weapon. But now I have to pick and choose, which is tough because there are so many options. You also can’t holster your weapon anymore, and Rico is officially always on edge now. I also feel like the old (JC3) map was more memorable, with landmarks I could recognize and say, “Oh hey, I know where I am.” But in JC4, the map is so large that every place I go feels new or like I've never been there before. It’s not too big a deal, but it can be overwhelming sometimes. As I mentioned in my last update, Everything feels just a little off. JC3 hit the vibe perfectly. gameplay, UI, and mechanics. And while JC4 is right there with it, it somehow misses the mark. Don't get me wrong, I love this game. But compared to JC3, when I’m playing, I get the feeling that “something's missing”. It's probably something to do with the new territory system. Now, while I quite enjoy it, I miss the gameplay mechanic where you could capture a base, destroy it, and see it marked as reclaimed on the map, with your previous destruction remaining. Adding to this, they removed the ability to freely claim regions and destroy bases. Long gone are the requirements to blow up a base. I understand that JC4’s gameplay isn’t meant to be like that, but at least repaint or remove targets once a region is claimed. Another pet peeve of mine, is that planes don't really shut down, which is pretty annoying… thus, if you land and park up, it just slowly keeps moving forward. On another note, the weather was kind of underwhelming… I liked the tornado mission, that was fun. But the main selling point of this game was so unimportant that I barely came across it during gameplay. But, on some high notes, I do enjoy the small frontline battle portrayed at the edges of your fronts. There's flak, tanks, and checkpoints set up. Writing of tanks, personally if any game has military vehicles, 9 times out of 10, it wins me over. And these new vehicles are very well thought out and designed. Each has some character or purpose behind it, and I really appreciate that. And while I’m still getting used to the fact that you can’t drop 4 items anymore, I do like the ability to set a loadout for each pilot. Very convenient! I also like the new parachute animation. It looks more realistic and physics-based. But even with this new animation, I thought my rocket-powered wingsuit wasn’t making a return, but my beloved Bavarium Wingsuit did come back! I also find Rico’s (somewhat) random voice lines (especially “Ride Of The Valkyries” one) very entertaining. Theres also a bunch of random events making the game more lively, along with plenty of well-animated cutscenes. So for now, I rest my case. I shall return once i’ve completed the main story :)

I'll start with addressing the fact that this game is not as good as Just Cause 3. I can't fully put into words how, but a lot of what it does just doesn't feel as fun as the chaos that was Just Cause 3. 4 attempted to be more grounded, I would say. At least in terms of story. Your introduction to 3 was standing on top of a plane with a rocket launcher with infinite ammo, blowing up everything in sight. It was insane, over the top, and everything that Just Cause needed to be. Just Cause 4 starts with climbing a big tower.
There are a lot of other ways that Just Cause 4 fails where 3 succeeded, some things just didn't flow as well, didn't feel as fun. 3's story was never going to win any awards, it wasn't exactly War and Peace, but it got the job done, and it wasn't bad. It felt unintrusive, you could enjoy it if you wanted to, but if you didn't care, no problem. 4's felt like it had poorer writing, the characters were forgettable, kind of annoying in some cases, and the story just didn't feel as interesting while also being a lot more in your face.
Despite all this though and many other things, I'm still recommending this game. Why? Because even if it isn't 3, it's still fun. It's a game that you can enjoy, even if it's far from perfect. There are a lot of changes to the game that I didn't care for compared to three, but also a lot of new things they introduced that I really like. The new grappling system is a lot of fun to play around with, already having ten hooks giving you a lot of potential to mess with things. The new weapons are fun, with their secondary fires being interesting and able to change the game flow. I still miss the eDEN Spark, but there's also a lighting gun in this game, too. They added a lot of new vehicles, and a radio in cars, which is fun, and it's great to have tanks with actual treads this time. While the map may not be as pretty or interesting as Medici, I did appreciate how it had different biomes and looked different in other areas, and the graphics are really good, too. While I prefer the old liberation and mission system, I did find it interesting how taking over a base would also involve some kind of task to complete. They could get repetitive and some of them just kind of sucked, but it was still interesting, and some tasks were actually fun. With a redesign, I think it could work. The rebel drops in this game also felt a lot more precise and useful, which is saying something because they were already very useful in 3.
I think how this could all be summed up as while 4 changed a lot of things for the worse compared to 3, it also introduced a lot of new things that I had a lot of fun with, and I still find myself sometimes coming back to this game to mess around with them. If there ever is a Just Cause 5, I'd hope the developers can learn from both their mistakes and wins in this game and design something that had the foundation of something like 3, with all the fun innovations 4 had. That's what sequels are meant to be, if you asked me. Building on each other.

Just Cause 4 is much like the previous games in the series, with tons of vehicles, aircrafts, guns and all kinds of gadgets, including your trusted grappling hook, parachute and jet pack. All of this makes for a really cool and truly action filled game! All though the history is a bit thin, the missions are really cool, and you're almost free to do whatever you want with this game! There are even some secret things hidden in the game too! 

I have really enjoyed the games in the Just Cause 4 series, and all though they are all different, the goal is the same. Create chaos, destroy things, and make for a better place, wherever you are...at least for yourself!

With a great variety of challenges, missions and overall tons of things to do, I was really happy with what the game could offer. On the other hand, what I liked really much for the previous just cause games, were challenges that were actually challenging. I remember especially the wingsuit challenges in previous games, that had more than 3 rings, and required some practice to get through some times. 3 rings for the wingsuit challenges was not always simple to do, but I would rather have a long track, like with the hooverboard. I really enjoyed the achievements in Just Cause 4, because they were all mostly unique, and they were fun to do too!

There are only a couple of things that I disliked a bit in the start. You're taking over land, not bases, but I figured this worked out in the end, because to gain chaos, you still need to destroy things. I still found previous games where you actually took over bases more fun, even though it could sometimes be tedius to find the small thing you didn't blow up. On the other hand, taking over land, while destroying whatever you want to do, makes for faster progress, and that's not bad either. So not a big problem overall, with such a great game!

I was also a bit annoyed over that I was not able to change the keys of the wingsuit, because it was inverted, but as I had no choice other to deal with it, and live with, that is just what I did.

It wouldn't be fair to not recommend this game, but in all fairness, the earlier games were better. I saw my playtime for Just Cause 2, and it has 50 hour more time played, compared to this one. It's still worth playing, since it's in the series, and I do recommend it.

This game gets a bad rap because it's a downscale from JC3, but that doesn't mean it's not a great game.
I went in to scratch the itch of driving around blowing stuff up, and JC4 delivers exactly that, so I was certainly not disappointed.

It's a bit more sandboxy than JC3 because capturing regions require you to get squads, which you get by causing Chaos (i.e. blowing stuff up). So you can capture a region without even setting foot in it, though some regions require a specific operation without them to be done before you can capture them - but they're always available, versus only available after you destroyed all enemy assets in the region.
I read some players dislike that approach compared to JC3, on my side I do like it better because that gives you freedom in how you want to approach capturing a region. I got way more than enough squads just playing the game naturally, and before capturing a region I usually went in with a chopper or tank to destroy all the assets I could find (usually in parallel to doing the region-specific operation) just for the fun of blowing stuff up.

You also get mods for the grappling hook which are a fun idea, though a bit cumbersome to set up and use.

You do however feel that the game was a bit rushed, with expedited story lines and features, and a few bugs to overcome (like having to properly set processor affinity every time the game is launched, or fast travel displaying actual keybinds but still using original keybinds). Still very fun to play though!

DLCs are a mixed bag:
* Dare Devils is a hit or miss, I feel. I personally liked it because it's driving around blowing stuff up and that's my thing in Just Cause. If you dislike vehicle handling and physics in JC you might not have a good time though.
* Los Demonios is a great idea but terrible execution. Everything about it was frustrating gameplay to me, starting with the fact you can't use vehicles at all in that DLC which is a huge turn off for me. Add to that a constant supply of flying pestering enemies that suicide-explode on you and tanks blasting you off the sky and you get a frustrating combat experience.
* Danger Rising was okay. It's driving around blowing stuff up so I can't complain. I disliked the DLC vehicle (hoverboard) so your mileage may vary depending on that, especially since it adds hoverboard races which were among my worst experiences in that game. Endless respawning enemies is more or less okay, not so when there are many AA turrets around that you can't destroy with respawning enemies constantly going back to man them.

Overall: I wanted to blow stuff up, JC4 gave me stuff to blow up, I was happy. Less good than JC3, still a great game.

[✔️] 🌆 Beautiful World: The environment is expansive, featuring diverse landscapes from lush jungles to massive deserts. The visuals are gorgeous, with impressive details on the world’s design.
[❌] 🌧️ Inconsistent Weather Effects: While the dynamic weather system is a cool idea, it often feels overblown, with storms and wind effects becoming more of a distraction than an enhancement.

[h2] Gameplay and Mechanics [/h2]

[✔️] 🧨 Explosive Action: As with other Just Cause titles, the game is full of chaotic action, including car chases, explosions, and massive set-pieces. The grappling hook and wingsuit are still fun and satisfying to use.
[❌] 🎮 Repetitive Missions: The missions can become repetitive quite quickly. The formula doesn’t vary much, and many of the objectives feel like a rehash of previous games in the series.
[❌] ⚙️ Sluggish AI: The AI can feel dumb at times, with enemies either failing to notice you or making strange decisions that hinder immersion.

[h2] Story and Narrative [/h2]

[❌] 📖 Weak Story: The narrative is forgettable and doesn’t offer anything new to the series. While Rico’s personal motivations are explored, the overall story feels generic and doesn't really drive the action forward.
[❌] 🎭 Bland Characters: The characters, especially the main villain, lack depth and charisma, which makes it hard to care about the stakes of the story.

[h2] Audio and Sound Design [/h2]

[✔️] 🎵 Great Soundtrack: The music is fitting and adds to the intensity during action sequences, with a mix of upbeat and suspenseful tracks.
[❌] 🔊 Generic Voice Acting: The voice acting doesn’t stand out and feels a bit flat, which, combined with the weak story, makes it harder to invest in the characters.

[h2] Content and Replayability [/h2]

[✔️] 🔄 Plenty of Side Content: The open world is filled with collectibles, challenges, and activities, giving players reasons to explore and complete the game fully.
[❌] 🎮 Lacks Innovation: While there’s plenty to do, the gameplay doesn’t offer much new compared to previous entries. It feels like a retread of old ideas rather than introducing fresh concepts.

[h2] Pros and Highlights [/h2]

[✔️] 🧨 Explosive Fun: The chaotic gameplay is still fun, and the combination of weapons, vehicles, and gadgets provides moments of pure, unbridled excitement.
[✔️] 🌍 Beautiful World: The game’s open world is vast and visually stunning, offering a rich environment to cause chaos in.

[h2] Cons and Drawbacks [/h2]

[❌] 🧩 Repetitive Gameplay: Despite the open world and freedom to approach missions differently, the core gameplay loop becomes tedious after a while.
[❌] ⚡ Weak Story and Characters: The narrative and character development are lackluster, making it harder to get emotionally invested in the game.
[❌] 🎮 Underwhelming AI: The AI’s lack of intelligence and strange behavior can often break immersion.

[h2] Additional Comments [/h2]
Just Cause 4 is, unfortunately, the weakest entry in the series, failing to live up to the excitement and innovation that its predecessors brought. While the world is beautiful, and the chaotic gameplay is still fun, the repetitive missions, lack of a compelling story, and weak AI make it feel like a step backward for the franchise. However, it’s still an enjoyable experience if you’re looking for some mindless fun and explosions.

Just Cause 4 might just be one of the most fun games I’ve ever played. The combination of a grappling hook, wingsuit, and parachute creates an unmatched sense of freedom and creativity. Visually, Just Cause 4 shines. The graphics are stunning, and the lighting makes every environment pop. The map is one of the most diverse I’ve seen in an open-world game, featuring everything from dense jungles and serene forests to snowy mountains, sandy beaches, skyscrapers, grasslands, cordfields and farmhouses. Exploring this world never gets old, and the variety keeps it feeling fresh every time you play.
The challenges are another aspect that keeps me coming back. Wingsuit stunts, vehicle stunts, speed runs, hoverboard courses, races, and other DLC activities add layers of replayability. They’re both fun and rewarding, pushing you to master the mechanics while having a blast.
Honestly, I often boot up Just Cause 4 just to explore the map with the wingsuit. There’s something incredibly satisfying about soaring through the skies, zipping between cliffs, or gliding over the ocean. It’s pure freedom, and the game does an amazing job of making traversal itself a form of entertainment.
If you’re looking for a game where you can unleash chaos, explore a gorgeous and varied open world, and have endless fun with creative tools and mechanics, Just Cause 4 is a must-play. It’s a game that doesn’t take itself too seriously, and that’s exactly what makes it so memorable.

Probably I’m writing this too late for most of you… the game has been out awhile.  I got this on Humble some time ago, and it sat there gathering dust until one day I decided to play JC3.  But I pressed the wrong install button and ended up playing JC4.  I am a JC newb.  I played JC2 once many years ago, but I won’t be comparing this game to previous entries in the series.

This game is super fun.  It’s an action movie in video game format.  The hero you play is named Rico because of course it is.  He has a perpetual 5 o’clock shadow, and confronts enemies with his signature leather jacket (sleeves rolled up… naturally...  Rico is a man who gets to work) and worn-in jeans.  He has holsters crisscrossing his torso.  He speaks in English but with a manly Spanish accent (which probably should have been Austrian in keeping with the action hero genre).   And with his wingsuit, grappling hook, and parachute, he can do all sorts of moves not permitted by physics.  He’s basically spider-man.  That’s one of his super-powers.  The other is that he is practically immune to bullets.

There’s plenty of gunplay to be had, and all that is really fun, but the game is really about movement.  Nothing beats using his grappling hook shoot him over the heads of his enemies while they voice their amazement.  It took me a little bit to get used to the movement mechanics.  Early on, the game introduces timed missions.  These were frustrating; it took me about 15 tries to complete the first one.  But once I had the hang of it, the timed missions were no big deal.  I do admit to nearly rage quitting on the second timed mission.

The game gives you about 10 mission types (+3 more with the DLC) on repeat.  There’s two variations of timed missions, defend the base, snipe the bad guys, find the right vehicle to gain entry into the stronghold, turn off the switches, destroy the McGuffin, etc..  Then there are a bunch of little missions like wingsuit through the rings within a time limit, drive really fast through a checkpoint, crash a car – those latter ones can be completely ignored without impacting the game in any meaningful way (which I did).  The DLC missions, particularly the one about the bugs, offer more challenge, but in a good way.  Once of the DLC is a racing mini-game – but I got motion sick playing it, so that was that.

I had a great time playing the action hero.  I loved Rico’s almost irritated grunts when perforated by shrapnel.  Rico and his allies have an army, but he always goes it alone, flying into heavily defended locales, murdering his enemies, and securing his objective.  Then, moving on to the next one.  Despite the repetitiveness of the missions, I never got bored.  I loved improving my skills around Rico’s movement --  I got a Serotonin jolt every time I executed a particularly slick move.

Highly recommend this for people who like the 3rd-person action genre, particularly if you prefer games that prioritize senseless violence over story.

As a fan coming off of Just Cause 3, I can understand the frustration at release, especially with how the marketing material presented the game as far more than what it's worth.
As is typical for Western games, the game also released broken and unfinished.
I got it years after release for chump change, and with all patches and DLC.

Ultimately, this game isn't as good as the predecessor, but a lot of it is down to personal preference.

First,
[h2] The Cons [/h2]
Let's get the elephant out of the room: The downgrade in GRAPHICS and PHYSICS is laughable.
However, I think one needs to understand that, unlike the predecessor, this game wasn't made with Unreal Engine 4, but Avalanche's proprietary Apex tool. Which is to say, a lot of time and money that could have gone into development was siphoned by making this tool. I imagine they didn't use UE4 because of licensing fees.

The SOUNDTRACK suffered, too.
But again, Avalanche can't really be blamed. You can beat Henry Jackman, who composed Just Cause 3 alongside Zach Abramson, and I imagine Jackman doesn't charge pennies either.
However, Abramson has done as good of a job as he could to learn from working with Jackman, and I think the effort should be complimented. The adaptive mixing is also back and better.

Personal Issue: The WINGSUIT CONTROLS are easier.
It was quite fun to spend hours crashing in Just Cause 3, but now being able to look back at just how good I've gotten at daring wingsuit maneuvers. It seems that in Just Cause 4, your wingsuit loses momentum much slower, and thus, the experience is also not as kinetic, since the momentum simulates wind resistance, and you hardly feel any of that here.

Now,
[h2] The Pros [/h2]
The STORY is a mixed bag, but generally, I prefer it.
While Just Cause 1 and 2 were not to be taken seriously at all, 3 did have some important and personal beats, and generally communicated its theme rather well.
Di Ravello was also, while generic, a good dictator antagonist.
Here, both villains, Oscar Espinoza and Gabriela Morales, are eternally in the background and hardly interact with the characters. Especially Gabriela, being the sister of Rico's friend and sister in arms Mira, has so much missed potential.
However, Oscar Espinoza ties very well into both Rico's personal history, as well as that of the country of Solis, and is generally interesting because of that. I just wish we'd actually gotten to see him act like the crybaby which he looks like. I do like that he's an oligarch who uses a mercenary army, though, as both of those things are underexplored in ficiton inspired by contemporary politics. Like how Di Ravello served as a baseline example for fascism, Espinoza does for oligarchy.
The sci-fi tech is kind of out of the blue here, as, while it was already present in 3, there it had a coherent theme that suspended the audience's disbelief, that being the mineral Bavarium, which only existed in its ficitonal country of Medici.
Here, the Black Hand just have all sorts of insane sci-fi weapons, tools, vehicles etc., just 'cause Espinoza has unlimited money and can buy stuff from wherever he wants.

I really like the other CHARACTERS.
I found most characters in 3 to be pretty damn annoying (except for the radio propaganda guy, David Tennant), and I like how much of the personalities of 4's cast tie into your interactions with them.
The new radio propaganda isn't as funny as Tennant's was, but I like it being a talkshow where the hosts, Thiago and Santiago, legitimately believe the garbage their script says.
There's Sargento, the strategist of the Army of Chaos, who coordinates the army behind the back the one-man-army that is Rico. He's inexperienced, but he's got heart, and Rico inspiring and teaching him is cool.
Javi is an archaeologist who used to perpetuate the Espinoza dynasty's propaganda about how they were supposedly the ones who had been improving Solis in the centuries since the Conquistado Diego Espinoza de Malaga arrived, and who, after being locked up for getting sick of lying, now tasks Rico to help him uncover the relics of the last dynasty of indigenous ancient Solino rulers, in order to prove Espinoza a liar.
My favorite is Garland King, who is just female Michael Bay from New York and who wants to Rico to be her stuntman in what I can only assume to be the most idiotic movie since Morbius. I love her.

Many disagree, but I actually like that you take over BASES by completing certain tasks now, instead of just destroying all the chaos objects.
They are, of course, a staple of the series, and their meaning has now been reduced so much that they even respawn upon restarting the game, but the developers at least found some good use for them, which is that they make the arcade-style score counter relevant again, by essentially acting as experience points. Every time you fill the chaos meter, you get an additional squad of insurgents, which you need to take over more areas.

The new GRAPPLING HOOK is also cool.
Random tasks which you are given while exploring the map are nice, and they reward you by unlocking mods for your grapple, depending on which character gave you the task. It gives you a lot more to do while randomly exploring.

The DLC for this game is much better than the undercooked additons of 3.
While they added cool mechanics and expanded on the lore, 3's DLCs were really just tacked on.
4's three DLCs all add new missions all over the map which completely switch up your gameplay and have their own themes.

[h2] Verdict:
Some things better, some things worse, but generally overhated. Buy on sale if interested. Better with mods.

The central plot has you dive into the eye of a tornado, wingsuit through a thunderstorm, and drive a train through a sandstorm. It honestly rules! I loved it.

The Bad: The 3 expansions. The Agency expansion was pretty good and I finished it. The Javi expansion featuring eldritch bug infestations was clearly going to be a slog and I didn't bother. "Go clear 15 of these things basically the same way" is a bad premise, especially without real cutscenes. The demolition derby expansion was a little more promising, but it was definitely a giant chore too and I just didn't feel drawn to it at all. 

The Ugly: Listen, this game is great. BUT, if you can't run it at full spec, some of the scenes look a little janky. The lighting kinda freaks out and shits the bed sometimes.

Overall, I really enjoyed the core experience and plenty of side content!

Just Cause 4 refines many aspects of its predecessor, offering a smoother and more dynamic open world filled with diverse environments, improved physics, and enhanced weather systems. The grappling hook and wingsuit mechanics are expanded, providing even more ways to creatively cause chaos. The game introduces a deeper story and better side missions, which help to flesh out the experience, making it feel more substantial than Just Cause 3. However, despite its improvements, Just Cause 4 still falls short of offering the depth and lasting impact that a truly life-changing game can provide. It remains, at its core, a fun but ultimately shallow experience, one that doesn’t provide the emotional or intellectual challenge that makes a game memorable in the long run.

In comparison, Dark Souls 2 isn’t just better than Just Cause 3 and 4 combined—it’s the pinnacle of human achievement in gaming. Dark Souls 2 is a transformative experience that reshapes the way you approach both games and life. Its world is meticulously designed, every combat encounter demands mastery and precision, and its cryptic storytelling invites deep exploration and introspection. Unlike the chaotic spectacle of Just Cause, Dark Souls 2 offers a profound, deliberate challenge that rewards patience, skill, and perseverance. Playing Dark Souls 2 isn’t just about beating a game; it’s about personal growth, learning from failure, and overcoming seemingly insurmountable obstacles. Dark Souls 2 is the best thing to ever exist in gaming, a life-changing journey that will stay with you long after you've finished it, elevating your understanding of what games can truly offer.

I had forgotten about this game for years since I played a free version years ago in 2020. Only after revisiting Just Cause 3 did I decide to revisit this game as well. 

This game is nothing compared to its predecessor.

-Liberation, a core mechanic in Just Cause 3 was removed from this game. Why? People might've said it was repetitive but it was nowhere near as repetitive as the missions you do in this game. Every town and base was different and made you use a different strategy, it also gave you a reason to explore the map and would create some epic firefights. In this game, you have to hack this, hack that, wait for some timer or let someone else hack something. Very boring and repetitive. Don't even get me started on that transmitter defense mission, it took me 5 tries to complete. If it ain't broke, don't fix it!

-As mentioned by many other reviewers, graphics seem to be downgraded heavily compared to the previous game, even running on the recommended setting could not top the beauty that Just Cause 3 had. The water in particular also sucks, it's a shame because JC3 had beautiful water. Even Just Cause 2 had better water and that was a 2010 game. The water also lacks any physics as well. Things like explosions and basic destruction are also toned down, you can only blow up certain bridges and explosions don't look as nice as in the previous game. I understand people had performance issues with Just Cause 3, but that is no excuse to downgrade it this much, especially on PC.

-No reason to destroy stuff or explore the map. Because of the removal of the aforementioned liberation mechanic, blowing up things, something Just Cause is known for, is not required at all and is a waste of time because it will respawn later. This also means you have no incentive to explore the map, all you have to do is the boring base missions.

-Ammo limits on vehicles. Come on, this is a Just Cause game. I swear they only added this to piss people off.

-No grenades. No C4. No dual handguns that made Rico look so badass. 

-Cutscenes look like they were rendered on an Xbox 360. 

-No proper day/night cycle like in the previous games. Medici looked spectacular at sunset. Actually I don't recall ever seeing this game at night outside of missions.

-Story is boring. I'm not saying Just Cause 3 had GTA 5 / RDR 2 levels of storytelling but at least that game had memorable characters (like Mario Frigo) and had a good dictator, Di Ravello. The game balanced serious moments with comedic and funny ones. As another reviewer put it, "at least JC3 acknowledged Di Ravello's presence and he was a thought out character." Meanwhile, none of the characters in this game are particularly memorable and the main dictator, Oscar Espinosa is only seen twice, once at the beginning, and once at the end. In addition, the story is now too serious, the comedic moments are gone. 

-No introduction and no final boss fight. JC2 and 3 both had introductions that were fun and epic. Firestarter playing and then launching rockets off a plane was badass. In this game, there is no introduction, it cuts to the chase immediately.
Also, there is no final boss fight, it is a cutscene instead. Fighting Panay and Di Ravello was fun, I don't understand why we couldn't have the same here.

-Heat is not fun anymore. In the previous game, you had actual heat levels (1 to 5) and the military would chase you. As the heat increased, they gradually bring more and more reinforcements, and then send in helicopters and tanks to try and stop you. It felt amazing blowing up every soldier trying to chase you.
In this game however, there are no more heat levels. It wouldn't be bad if the game didn't spam Black Hand units behind you. As the heat rises, helicopters and tanks show up like they did in the previous game, however in this game jets will also attack you. What's the big deal you ask? Well, there is no reliable way to fight back against these jets, they are overpowered too, usually almost killing you. To add insult to injury, the game will not stop spamming enemies and spawning them wherever you can't see, often right next to you. If you are in the air, fighter jets will spawn instantly. They somehow managed to swarm a remote island far from the mainland with their cars tanks and helicopters. Also, it breaks the immersion of a revolution when the Black Hand can chase you deep into Army of Chaos territory, which makes no sense.
At least in Just Cause 3 they spawned realistically, you could see the military driving down the road to intercept you.

-Frontlines are a classic example of 'good in theory, bad in practice'. The only practical use I found was to farm Chaos.

-I didn't even bother with challenges. Yes, they're as bad as people say they are. 

-Just Cause 3 had a beautiful and vibrant color tone that made it so nice to look at. In my opinion its beauty rivals big dogs like GTA 5. Just Cause 4 lacks this and the game looks pretty bland because of it.

-No incentive to drive vehicles. Just Cause 3 had the 'chop shop' challenges, allowing you to collect all sorts of vehicles. This game lacks that. Why drive when you can fly or fast travel?

-Vehicle physics suck, worse than the previous games actually. Don't get me started on motorcycles. 

-Map feels empty. Towns and cities don't feel alive. In Just Cause 3 towns felt alive, after liberating them there would even  be fireworks and street musicians performing.

-Enemy AI sucks. Some enemies are bullet sponges while others are just plain annoyances. 

-AI actually sucks in general. I could not complete several missions because some NPC wanted to go somewhere else instead of where the mission told me to go.

-The map is less interesting than previous games. I did explore the map, but I found it to way more boring than exploring Medici or Panau. The desert for example is nearly empty.

-Base liberation missions are literally just copy paste recycled missions. 

-UI is trash.

-I nearly forgot about the disasters. They are only used in a few missions and most are then never seen again. Unacceptable, considering how much they featured in this game's marketing. Literally every trailer was just random dubstep music with a tornado or something.

-All DLC's are garbage and are a waste of time and money, except Danger Rising, which is surprisingly okay.

So, what about the pros?

-You can blow up stuff?

-Weapons are, alright?

-The map is, there?

TLDR/In conclusion this game was a major step backwards for its franchise, it's no wonder that this game was forgotten after about a year and that nobody, not even me remembers this game. Please, do yourself a favor and get Just Cause 3. You can thank me later. It's such a shame because this game had so much potential.

I just found this game... not fun... compared to Just Cause 3. I've barely spent a fraction of the time on it as I have in JC3 and I've already uninstalled and reinstalled twice. If you're reading this and ready to find my address to bash in my family's skulls with a pipe wrench in the dead of night, then consider hearing out my arguments below.

The additions to this game compared to the last are of minimal importance. New vehicles are kinda cool but redundant when the wingsuit is more versatile. New weapons are kinda cool but don't provide anything other than a greater extent of overkill. New storms are kinda cool but ultimately prove to just be eye candy (tornado) or an annoyance (all other weather). And new grapple abilities are kinda cool if you go out of your way to use them instead of your exponentially more destructive weapons. I would assume that all the new toys exist to allow the player greater freedom and creativity in choosing their method of destruction, but unless you deliberately limit your options, the desire for creativity quickly goes out the window in favor of your portable WMDs. If anything, more options lead to less creativity because you'll never be in a situation where you don't have the perfect tool for the job.

Meanwhile, the change to the core gameplay loop of systematically liberating the country was not a change that needed to be made IMO. Liberating every named location in JC3 got tedious toward the end, but no more tedious than completing one of a small handful of BASIC mission types: this game's way of liberating the map. Any by "basic", I mean stuff like wave defense; that's just pure laziness! On the other hand, even more laziness might have been a better choice because I think the game would be improved by just recycling the liberation mechanics from JC3. Blowing up every single god damn red thing on the map got mind-numbing, but at least it provided brief moments of badass-ery when swooping in to utterly annihilate a unsuspecting outpost in seconds without ever touching the ground or, on rarer occasions, the hyperactive mega-explosion fuck-fest of destroying a whole port single-handedly while every carbon based life form in a 500m radius tries to snipe you out of the sky. Maybe other people play differently, but in this game I just avoid tackling big bases because they are no longer mandatory and I can fill my chaos bar up a lot more efficiently by just flying around and hammering any small installations I see.

I could go on but I'd prefer to go do something other than feverishly tap out my feelings for a barely AAA game (despite how cathartic it was), so I'll leave you with this: If you wanted more Just Cause 3 but bigger and better then this might be the game for you. But it probably isn't.

Nothing works like the previous and well working games. Everything was changed and for the worse. In [b]Just Can't 4[/b] they doubled down on the controls so that many of the buttons need two functions, just so they could cram more things in. "Just Cause" and "buttons-galore" are not two things that belong in the same sentence. It's like the devs noticed there is thing called keyboard and they could cram more things into it then previously!

I can imagine the discussion:
Director: I want buttons for everything.
Coders: Everything..?
Director: EVERYTHING!!!
Coders: How about two functions for every button!?
Director: *heavy breathing*

The functions are scattered all around the keyboard with little logic. You need several hours to just learn and memorize the buttons and their functions. As a little example, the control options lists 4 different buttons for "next menu" and "previous menu". Where is that menu? It's button "1" where it previously was in "Tab". And the grab hook? They changed it from "mouse right" because heck, why not! It's only the most used thing in the game! "Right mouse" has now zoom aim. And that "mouse right" has to have two modes, press and hold, just so they could get more things in! And if you happen to have machine gun with a shield, it's a third button for one gun plus the mandatory reload button! And that previously working grab hook, the biggest and funniest thing in Just Cause-games..? There is now half a dozen buttons for it! You apparently can't tighten the tether yourself anymore, it does it automatically. But there is now two buttons for "quick-reel" because that was apparently a priority. Previously used "F" for throwing grenades was changed to the industry standard "Middle Mouse". Why? So they could cram more buttons for that "F"!!!

And all in all, everything that previously nice and neat, is now menus, CONSTANT mayhem (whether you wanted or not) and idiotic controls because .. i don't know. They like it confusing. It's not like nobody wanted to play a fun and casual game like Just Cause. More convenient to take button controls, mix them up in a bag and throw them to table and see how confusing they could make everything. I'm not going to spend hours to just get this game playable in menus and with mods, this game is dead to me. Make the next Just Cause like JC2 or JC3 and i'll consider buying. With big reservations.

As a huge fan of Just Cause 3, I went into Just Cause 4 expecting an even crazier, more explosive sandbox experience. Instead, I got a dull, lifeless game that stripped away everything that made its predecessor fun.

Right from the start, JC4 felt off. The vibrant, chaotic Mediterranean setting of JC3 is replaced with an uninspired world filled with endless, repetitive lush forests that lack personality. The game takes itself way too seriously, completely missing the over-the-top charm that made JC3 such a joy to play.

And then there’s the gameplay… or rather, the struggle to stay entertained. After a few missions, I realized how monotonous and uninspired the game had become. The missions are bland, the destruction feels nerfed, and the physics—arguably one of the best parts of JC3—have been dumbed down. Even the new weather mechanics, which seemed promising, add little to the experience beyond gimmicky set pieces.

I couldn't even be bothered to finish the game, let alone consider purchasing the DLCs. If JC3 was a thrilling, explosive action movie, JC4 is a watered-down sequel that forgot what made the franchise fun in the first place. A massive disappointment.

I was really let down by this entry in the series. It's riddled with bugs, from vehicles freaking out and stuttering all over the place, to randomly clipping through the world, or just random things not working in general. In just 2 hours of playing this game, I saw more bugs than I have in games releasing in alpha with a single developer.
Not only is the game buggy, but the AI is as dumb as a bag of rocks, and they all share a single brain cell. I don't think the AI even knows how to fly helicopters. I've seen them crash into each other, the ground, or anything and everything else around them. When driving, they will straight up drive off cliffs to their death at full speed. I had 3 or 4 in a row drive off one after the other while chasing me, and I didn't even lead them to it.

When it comes to gameplay, it just sucks. I was constantly running out of ammo, and collecting data was extremely frustrating. You can't cancel it, it resets any time you get shot or knocked off of it, and it takes a solid 10 seconds of waiting for the AI to spawn before I'd be able to finish collecting the data. They would then shoot me, causing it to reset again. Having to do that 3 or 4 times each time I had to collect data wasn't fun. The flight controls for the helicopters are horrible as well, and it's not something that you can just fix by changing your controls. It's just how the game is. Unlike most games where you'd expect using your mouse to rotate the helicopters, it doesn't, or it does but really slowly. So rotating around is slow and clunky. It's also really stupid that the AI will shoot missiles at their own helicopters if you're hanging from them. Every time I tried to hijack a helicopter, by the time I'd reach it, it would immediately be hit and take damage.

Another thing that I found frustrating is how many AI they will send after you. You can be swarmed in seconds by a couple helicopters, jets flying overhead dropping bombs, and trucks with mounted guns firing at you. You get overwhelmed so quickly, and when you're just starting out, it isn't fun.

The game also doesn't like showing or telling you what you're supposed to be doing. After completing every mission, I'd be left confused, wondering if I was actually done or not since nothing would pop up or there'd be no dialogue telling me either. If you use the new AR thing that's supposed to light up objectives, it really isn't that helpful and only does anything when the game tells you to use it.

The menus are also confusing and the controls are weird. Why can't I just press "ESC" to go back? Why does it have to be only the delete button? "1" and "2" open the loadout menu, which is another thing that just doesn't work how you'd normally expect it to. When customising loadouts, you have to press and hold enter while using A and D to switch between options. I've never seen any game do their menu like this before. Even navigating the map or the UI in general just doesn't feel right.

I normally don't care about graphics that much, but for a Just Cause game, it is kind of expected to look good. And for something that came out in only 2018, even on very high settings, it looked like Just Cause 2 on the Xbox 360. I was also sad to discover that unlike in Just Cause 3 where you can take down entire bridges, we're back to not being able to do that again, which was one of my favourite things to do. What surprised me the most was how badly the cut scenes looked, somehow they looked worst, it was like I was watching someone else playing the game but on the lowest settings it could have been set to. They should have just animated them instead of doing it all in engine, I know that would have been extra work but at least it would have looked good, unlike what's in the game now. 

For only around 2 hours of playing this game, I had to compress my list of complaints down to a few main points. Overall, I was really let down by this game. It just feels like a cheap knockoff. Even though I bought this game on sale, I'm still going to try and refund it. Even at a price tag of $5 for the base game, and a couple dlc packs, it's just not worth the time to play the game, even if this game was free I'd still avoid it.

I almost wish Steam had a "recommend if on sale for xx%", but since not I had to vote No. This one was frustrating, as there are clear improvements that are overshadowed by confusing downgrades. 
[u]PROS[/u]
- gunplay feels quicker and a little more frantic
- enemies move around more, especially helicopters, feel a bit more aggressive
- visuals are pretty, if oversaturated
- the tether is a little snappier when transitioning to a landing

[u]CONS[/u]
- no more base liberation (this was what I did the most JC3; re-oppress and fast travel to capture bases again, it was the main challenge of the game)
- challenges are basically gone. Instead of a full, beautiful wingsuit course, you have literally have "fly through 3 rings in less than 9 seconds". Instead of a race, you have "pass through this ring over 150 km/h". These are a joke I would expect from a single-person indie game, especially after JC3
- no longer have remote mines
- only two weapons can be equipped at once; no longer have dual-wield pistols/smgs

[u]OTHER[/u]
- control changes, the most subjective part:
 -- the d-pad no longer handles weapons. Left/Right now swap between your three tether loadouts, and Up to trigger effects
 -- weapon swapping is handled by holding Reload, hence only having two weapons now
 -- zoom-in moved from R3 to L2, and now must be held down, fine with me 
- you now have three different tether effects:
 -- Air Lift: attaches a lift balloon
 -- Retractor: auto-retracts once attached to two things
 -- Booster: is booster
 -- You can set 0-3 effects on each loadout
 -- You can set these effects to trigger automatically, or by pressing d-pad up, or holding it. You can also set the intensity/strength or each effect
 -- There are also mods, such as making the balloons fly in a direction instead of hover, or pop when they reach full altitude, or change booster direction, etc

* You also run out of ammo easy because Heat (enemies looking for you and trying to kill you) is very hard to get rid of since ENEMIES SPAWN IN THIN AIR RIGHT BEHIND YOUR BACK. Not even joking. I was across a large river on a desolate hill side. I shot a rocket at an enemy tank across the river. Infantry enemy IMMEDIATELY SPAWNED NEAR ME. I thought I was nuts. So, I tried it again. This time, a motorcycle enemy spawned instantly on my side of the river. They don't even give the illusion of enemies chasing you; they just spawn them right on top of you behind the camera to hide it. So, it's difficult to lose heat. And, they keep ramping up the enemies as you kill them, so eventually you have TANKS, HELICOPTERS, etc spawning all over you! If you go hide in the forest, they still eagle eye you through the trees, too. So, good luck with that sh*t. It's absolutely bottom-barrel BS from the devs.

* And, speaking of BS, some moron at Avalanche seems to think everyone plays JC to muck around with the grappling hook, because they doubled-down on how convoluted it is in JC4. You can only carry TWO guns, but you get THREE load-outs for the grappling hook, where you can mix-n-match retractor, blimp and rocket booster mods.. and those mods have their own mods, like speed/strength of retraction, etc. People play JC to go blow sh*t up, so it boggles the mind that they'd spend so much time making the grappling hook even more gimicky than making the game more compelling to play. It reminds me of JC2 or JC3 where the devs had such a h***-on with doing stupid things with the grappling hook that like 1/2 the achievesments revolved around it, like "hang someone up and then shoot / kick them". Just absolutely dumb stuff you'd have to be extremely extra about. For some reason they think that's why people play JC, so that's what they focused on.. and the rest of the game is poorer for it.

* Then they decided the DLC needed more gimicky BS by throwing in a hoverboard which is annoying to use, and you're forced to use it in puzzles on ships.

* And that leads to Puzzles. So many BS puzzles. I just want to blow stuff up. But, you have 30 seconds to go here to unlock this, then you need to hoverboard over a bunch of switches in a place where it's easy to get stuck on crap within 15 seconds to unlock this, then you have 2 minutes to fly all over the place to flip several switches... I JUST WANT TO SHOOT THINGS I THE FACE AND BLOW **** UP! IT'S NOT ROCKET SCIENCE! For the love of god, why did they double-down on the puzzle BS?

* Well, at least you get something for all your hard work, right? I mean, stuff is destroyed, and... NOPE! The game auto-saves. If you quit and continue your game ALL THE STUFF YOU BLEW UP IS BACK. So, your actions have no impact on the game world in the long run.

* And, even MAIN OBJECTIVES have no impact. You not only took control of an area, but also took control of the drone production facility. Doesn't matter. TONS of enemy drones spawn around you in an AREA YOU CONTROL and absolutely wreck you. How? You took over the production facility. How is the enemy getting stronger when you're wiping out and taking over all their stuff?! It makes absolutely no sense, and underlines that YOUR HARD WORK AND ACTIONS DON'T MAKE A DIFFERENCE. Sure, a few friendlies are cruising around, and the frontline of the war has shifted. But, there's still TONS of enemies in areas YOU CONTROL. So, you can't do anything without getting swarmed. Makes no sense.

* There's the usual petty, insulting "challenges" padding the game world out, so they can brag about "hours of fun". Drive a certain car through a hoop, wing suit through some rings, etc. Bottom-barrel open world BS. Every now and then they'll have "kill this person" or "drive this person here". I wouldn't mind this if it upgraded Rico and made him better. Like, better weapons, armor, etc. NOPE! You only gain XP to unlock mods for your grappling hook to make it more convoluted. It just reminds you that some dev at Avalanche got off on how great the grappling hook was by trying to cram it down your throat.

* They do have some interesting main missions....until you realize it's a "did you enjoy that 30 min mission? Well, you get to do it 5 more times!" Again, typical Avalanche. They have a "free the hostages" mission which you get to do over and over again, b/c.. yeah, that won't get boring. Then they have a "guard the transmitter" mission where they throw tons of enemies at you that chew the transmitter apart in no time, so you fail it over and over again until you finally give up and uninstall the game. NO JOKE! You'll die a few times, then quit the game, and google to see if it's just you.. and reddits and such are FULL of folks getting demolished on this mission. It's not a fun or challenging mission. It's just an abusive "F U" from the devs who seem to not play test of QA their game, and/or think making the player fail a mission over and over again against impossible odds is some how "compelling gameplay". And, if you make it past 1 of those.. guess what.. you got more to do, because of course you do, because Avalanche loves to puppy-mill out the same stuff over and over. Good luck!

There are moments when this game shines.. like shooting out a tire and watching an enemy vehicle flip, or when everything's blowing up and you're having a blast.

But, you spend more time frustrated with stupid puzzles, unfair enemy respawns, etc than having fun, especially when (like JC 2) heat takes forever to die down (and they start rolling in tanks in like 2 minutes!) causing you to run away with your tail between your legs instead of taking everyone on like a bad-***.
