A game that could have theoretically been fun, brought down constantly by the many, many broken elements.

It's not all bad. The basic movement is snappy on land, the soundtrack is decent, I quite liked the colors and contrasts used, and I appreciated how human the characters felt - nobody was over-the-top bombasts, and it was nice.

But that's about all I can think of for the positives. For the negatives, we have the constant crashing, broken anti-aliasing that makes facial hair look awful, heat never going away unless you flee, and combat that manages to be consistently annoying no matter how you play it.

There's two particularly nasty factors I want to mention though. The first is the fact that blowing things up no longer seems to be a focus of almost any part of the game. Oh, sure, everything's made of propane and every car's a Pinto, but exploding stuff no longer integrates with... basically anything. There's gas and oil aplenty, but almost nothing in the game requires you to interact with it. The closest thing that does is that blowing things up very slowly fills a bar that lets you take over regions slightly easier every time you fill it up, but that's about it, and taking over regions is plenty easy even without filling it more than twice. This game took the decent-if-not-perfect fun that was JC3 region takeovers and turned them into missions that, while different on the surface, all had very similar gameplay and which all managed to be slogs.

The second is the weather. Because, damn, this could have been one hell of a selling point for this game as an advance over its successor. JC3 was [i]great[/i] at making blowing stuff up fun, and weather effects integrating with that could've upped the spectacle so much! But it just... doesn't. Weather effects seem largely limited to the story missions about them, and although you [i]can[/i] fire them off yourself afterwards, I can't imagine a scenario in which I'd care to, since doing so is as much a threat to yourself as it is any enemy. Not to mention you have to travel to one of a select few parts of the map to acquire the ability, and it only works once before you have to go back again!

There could have been a good game here, for sure. But it would have needed an extra year at minimum, and I have a feeling that even then the game suffered from some bad mismanagement. If you get this, I suggest waiting until it's $5 or less.

Boring, especially that on top of that you have the battles happening on the borders, which as far as i know are there just to exist - take part or not - it doesn't matter for unlocking the region.

tl;dr - JC4 is a technical improvement, but it is simply not as fun.
If you goal is to mindlessly blow stuff up and have fun, buy it. If you want to 100% the game, do not buy it.

If you love guarding missions, or missions that force you to stay in one place while NPCs "hack" systems while enemies pop in out of nowhere and attack you from all sides then buy this game. If you hated JC2 or JC3's more free flowing game play and wished that missions were absolutely required to take over an enemy facility then you will love this game. If you love needlessly complex systems that make game play frustrating while trying to deal with a chaotic game then you will love this game. If you love how enemy units would spawn in out of nowhere to attack you then you will love this game.
If the above sounds great, then buy the game now and ignore what I say below.

The good things from this game. I loved feeling like there was an actual revolution going on. Having revolutionaries join in the fight was nice. It really felt like you were fighting a battle to free people. The past games felt like a solo war with the occasional battle with incompetent NPCs that I largely ignored. As cool as this is, it just becomes background noise after a while.

I like that there are weapons with so many different neat features. The gun that turns into a shielded turret and the guns with various explosive weapons. They are kind of fun. But I also miss having separate grenades and various explosive weapons.

The really big, annoying thing is the missions. I loved the free flowing nature of the previous games. I could approach capturing the map however I pleased. Now I have to perform missions to capture virtually every part of the map. I hated having to complete missions in JC2&3, but I did them when I had to. Missions are a major part of JC4.
You have to protect someone or something while waves of enemies swarm you or travel around activating things. There is some variations, but they are not terribly fun.

I miss having the supply drop available. Along with many of the things from JC3. The mechs and jet suite were fun. Yes, you can get them as overpriced DLC, but I won't. It is not a fun enough game to warrant buying it, at least at full price.

Long story short, am I happy with the game? I know that I am not enjoying it as much as JC2 or JC3. I have played 6 hours, and I am honestly getting tired of it already. It has some innovative and interesting things added to it. I wish that they would mix the good from the earlier games with the good from this one for future games. We will see if they do.

If you are going to buy it, buy it on sale. I don't recommend buying it at full price. If you love the series, then try it. If you are looking to get into it then buy JC2 or JC3, they are more fun.

At first glance, Just Cause 4 is stunningly beautiful and undeniably fun. The massive open world, filled with lush landscapes and explosive possibilities, promises endless hours of entertainment. The game's signature over-the-top action and creative use of the grappling hook initially deliver an exhilarating experience.

However, this potential quickly unravels due to one glaring flaw: the puzzles. The sheer volume of puzzles, combined with the lack of meaningful hints or guidance, makes progression a frustrating ordeal. The game often throws you into complex scenarios with no explanation, leaving you to fumble around until something works. This lack of clarity turns what should be a rewarding experience into a tedious chore.

Adding to the frustration is the overwhelming number of key controls. With so many functions mapped to different buttons, the game becomes needlessly complicated, especially for new players. Instead of feeling like a capable action hero, you're left wrestling with the controls in critical moments.

Ultimately, Just Cause 4 sabotages itself. What could have been an enjoyable, action-packed adventure is marred by poor design choices that prioritize complexity over fun. It's a shame, because the game's potential is undeniable—but it’s hard to appreciate when the experience is bogged down by unnecessary frustrations.

The good:
Graphics, sounds, voices, cutscenes, landscapes, a diverse world... A lot of work went into that. That's what makes it at least fun for a few hours.

The bad:
It's just... Empty. You keep blasting around, having fun with the parachute and the wingsuit, and hunt for story pieces... But everything is the same - just shoot and kill everything, until the thing says you're done. And then (other than in previous games) if you revisit the location, everything is built back up again! So it doesn't even matter. And as soon as you set foot in enemy territory, the sky is suddenly buzzing with ridiculous drones, planes and enemy helicopters, that came out of nowhere.

It's also buggy. I've experienced multiple CTD's, have had to reinstall because fullscreen didn't work any more, have had movement keys stuck, have glitched through vehicles, suddenly died out of nowhere, fell down from cliffs without taking a single hit, been unable to open or close the parachute... And then there's the servers being offline so I can't play, and then constantly mismatched cloud saves. It's just a mess. And that's all within 5 hours of playtime.

So yeah, it's a nope for me. I got it on sale for less than 10 bucks and what's 10 buck for a few hours of relative fun, so hey you can give it a try on a good sale, but the frustration about how badly the thing is put together just wins out.

Finished JC3 up to 100%, loved it for the crazy stunts and overall mayhem you can cause with your tethers, bavarium wingsuit and various explosives. I bought JC4 expecting a decent sequel and after a couple of hours posted this critic so... Let's see what I got.

[h1]Loyal to its older brother : 8/10[/h1]
JC3 was all about having fun with the unrealistic physics, grappling around and using your wingsuit to jump unsuspecting ennemies and destroy their whole base without them being able to do anything against you. And JC4 does it quite well. It even jump starts and bypasses the lengthy upgrading system in JC3 by giving you, right at the start of the game, 10 tethers (more than the 6 tethers limit in JC3) and in a couple of missions (less than 30 minutes of gameplay) provides you with the boosters and the air lifter. Overall, the reason I "only" gave it an 8/10 is because they unnecessarily changed the way you free the areas of the map. In JC3 you have to find several spots in each area, destroy all chaos objects and you were done. Here there is a bit less destruction involved and it is more like about completing certain missions, then ordering your "troops" to move in another area in which you will repeat the process. I think the idea was to make it feel like Rico needs the island's people to win but it sounds silly considering that the NPCs are just as useless as they were in JC3. Seriously, I just did a mission for which I need to take two NPCs with me drive in a car for several kilometers to destroy 4 boxes. It took me almost 10 minutes to get it done whereas doing it by myself with the wingsuit would have taken me less than 2 minutes. Basically you are still a one man army and you could install a mod that removes every member of the resistance and you wouldn't feel any difference. I think JC5, if it is made one day, should take this one man army seriously : the cutscenes should be about NPCs telling Rico that he needs their help to kill the evil dictator and Rico answering "Hey, I just destroyed 5 ennemy bases by myself without a scratch, don't worry about me, just stand back and enjoy the show".
Anyway, overall it is enjoyable, fun to play and the feeling is similar to what you had in JC3 between the gunfights, the wingsuit/parachute combo, the tethers and the handling of the fun and unrealistic physics.

[h1]Chaos mechanics : 4/10[/h1]
In JC3, the usual way you free an area was : head to this area, discover the N settlements in it (small bases, big bases, outposts...), destroy every chaos object in these settlements and the area becomes yours and the rebels now occupy these settlements.
In JC4, they removed this idea that you had to cause mayhem and destruction. Basically you do the 2 or 3 missions you can find in an area, during which you will have to kill black hand's soldiers, which generates chaos which grants you "rebel squads". These squads are "stored" somewhere in your... Inventory ? Whatever, basically you accumulate squads and once you have enough (between 2 and 4 for most areas) you click on the map to say "hey, rebels, go free this area", at which point the rebels establish a frontline where the constantly fight the black hand on the borders of this area. Then you do the missions in this area, accumulate a few more squads and proceeed to the next area. I do not like this idea, not only is it a fake way of pushing the idea that "Rico is just a man, he can't take the black hand by himself, he need help from the rebels who can't even kill a single foot-soldier in 5vs1 in less than 1 minute" even though you can move around freely on the whole map and utterly destroy any black hand squad you encounter. I really feel like the devs saw a few videos on youtube of players utterly destroying some black hand military bases and decided that "oh no, we can't have that, we need the player to work hand in hand with the rebels, it's much more realistic than a single man freeing a country !". I'm not exactly sure what was the motivation here, but it is a big failure, the amount of chaos you have to generate in "roaming" when you just mess with the black hand is absurd, i litterally spent 15 minutes destroying almost 50 helicopters and 50 armed cars and killing several soldiers, it only granted me 1/10th of a squad.

[h1]Graphics : 5/10[/h1]
Similar to JC3, graphics are not particularly great, personnaly I don't care about this in video games so it doesn't bother me. Just a quick note about the level design : the starting area (wachikuni, terra del qhapaq, hamparas...) looks a lot like what you can find in some parts of Ghost recon : Wildlands. 

[h1]Keyboard controls : 3/10[/h1]
Dear video games developers, for the last fucking time, no, no and no, I do not want, under any circumstances, to spend 15 minutes in the controls menu setting up my keys for walking, then for piloting a plane, then for piloting a helicopter, then for driving a car, then for FOR FUCK'S SAKE WHO IN THIS WORLD USES DIFFERENT MOVEMENT KEYS BETWEEN THEIR CHARACTER MOVEMENTS AND THE VEHICLE MOVEMENTS ??? I don't get it. I also do not want to have to go through the 13 different menus to see what action is the 'X' key bound to if I want to use it for something. Binding keys should not be that hard : you double click on an action, you press the key you want to attribute to this action, and if it is already bound the game either highlights the conflict or switches both keys. Then you display every action in the same menu with categories, you do not split it between 13 submenus.
While we are talking about the menus, if you have the sound and the sensitivity set as values between 0 and 100 (it goes even beyond 100 for the sensitivity, I don't understand how scales work in your minds but whatever), you either use a slider or provide us with an input to quickly change it, I don't want to hold my right arrow for 30 seconds to reach the value I want. 
Driving feels as weird as some of the games with the weird driving system I have ever seen like Ghost Recon: Wildlands and Watch Dogs 1. No intertia, your car's tires are basically made of oil, but frankly aside from missions that require me to use a car I stick to the good old wingsuit so it's not that much of a bother. 

[h1]Story : 0/10[/h1]
If you played JC3 for its story, you're weird. The story of JC3 was worthy of a very low-budget serie Z movie, and the same can be said for JC4. You start by attacking a base by yourself, you handle everything they throw at you, and suddenly cut-scene and you lose and get shot down. Had the game left the controls to you, the final boss would have been dealt with in less than 10 minutes. 
I rated it 0/10 but lets be frank, it is like rating minecraft's graphics 0/10 : the mark is deserved, but just like you're not supposed to care about minecraft's graphics, you're not supposed to care about Just Cause's story. It's a silly story that doesn't make the slightest sense, and it doesn't matter at all.

[h1]Overall : 1/10[/h1]
Had I posted this evaluation yesterday, the overall note would have been 7/10 and my explanation for it : 
[code]I wouldn't say it is a must play, but it is a decent sequel to JC3. About as fun as its older brother, JC4 is rather enjoyable but unless you are a hardcore fan of the series, I would advise to wait for some discount, I wouldn't considering spending more than 15-20€ for it.[/code]

The game's world feels very bland to me and doesn't speak much volume as 3 did. feels like a bad redo of Just Cause 2's world and nothing is very unique.

Graphics:

Performance: 
I have an RTX 3060Ti paired with an i7 12700f with 16Gb of 3200Mhz RAM.
This is by no means a top-notch setup, but it is well beyond to at least allow the game to run at 1440p, 120-100 FPS. But I can't, not at least at a steady 100. As a massive fan of the Just Cause series, I really wanted to like this game, but it thwarted my every attempt.

I'm assuming that you've played Just Cause 3 if you're reading this review and that you're trying to figure out if you'll like this game too. The short answer is no, you won't. On the other hand, if you're reading this and you haven't played Just Cause 3, then what are you doing? Go buy it on some $1 bundle deal, it's insane how cheap you can get it these days. Then you can come back and read this review.

Right, now that we're just down to the Just Cause 3 players, let's talk about expectations. Whatever the original Just Cause did, Just Cause 2 improved upon. The map was a massive improvement, the combat was an improvement, there are more easter eggs, more vehicles, and a much nicer quest system with well implemented factions among other things. Given that the original Just Cause released to PlayStation 2 among other consoles in 2006, Just Cause 2 arriving in 2010 was the first truly modern game in the series.

In December 2015, we got Just Cause 3. Avalanche Studios did a lot in that 5 year gap, improving on every system that was available in Just Cause 2, adding whole new mechanics and upgrades for the grappling hook to enable a whole new world of possibility. The beauty of the world was, and still is, staggering, as is its scale. Everywhere you went there was either something to see or do. The challenges were actually challenging, and the arcadey gameplay was actually fun.

I'm not normally the sort to enjoy hunting all the collectibles, getting all the achievements, completing all the time trials, or even competing on leaderboards with my steam friends for the in-game challenges. Yet I found myself doing that with Just Cause 3 just because it was such a fun game, and all those mechanics were integrated seamlessly. It was a fantastic addition to the Just Cause series and remains the best Just Cause game by far.

All of this context is necessary because if there was to be a Just Cause 4 (and there is), there needed to be a good reason for it. What might they improve upon in the next iteration? How did they plan to top Just Cause 3, releasing only 3 years after it? (Only 2 years if you count the time only after all the DLC content for JC3 had dropped)

It's a question with an easy answer. They changed the engine to something marginally different, they added over 400 challenges, turning them into a boring chore, they removed the vibrancy and colour from the game, opting to split the land into 4 environmental regions, and they made the most common/important mission type (liberations) dependent on an awful protect-the-idiot-ai system. Just Cause has never been a combat sim, it thrived on chaos and a bit of silliness. 

All that is to say, Just Cause 4 wasn't even remotely as much fun to play. Along with the engine changes, a lot of stuff just feels wrong too. Look, if you've played Just Cause 3 to death and you REALLY want more Just Cause, then fine. Grab a whiskey and sit down to to play Just Cause 4 with greatly lowered expectations. Grab the Danger Rising DLC so you at least have a hoverboard.

An absolute failure of a game from start to finish, I loved JC2 and enjoyed JC3 almost as much, but this game is just terrible and *consistently frustrating*.

All the mechanics we loved in the series, the destruction of bases to liberate territory, being able to mix in a bit of stealth with the run and gun, having a viable loadout for several types of missions, all that has been replaced with what I can only assume is the product of a Square-approved design committee who all hated fun.

My first two hours in this game was a comedy of broken gameplay, with me rage alt+f4'ing this monstrosity three separate times, along with two crashes to desktop.

For some reason, the menus are hard coded to the most arbitrary keys, with no real help, so when the game tried to show me the big complex menu for grapple tools and then crashed me halfway through the mission, I was stuck on coming back in since the menu for doing that got re-locked after the checkpoint.

Then you spend a half hour messing around getting supply and grapple stuff set up, and realize that even when getting a weapon resupply that there is no extra ammo with it, meaning that I end up setting all 3 pilots to the same item and dropping 3 so I can get stocked up.

The stunts and side quests are 100% garbage, the ones that aren't broken are just "find a vehicle and drive through this ring" and a lot of them are pretty broken, the driving and airsuit controls are horrid and feels like piloting an ocean liner that suddenly jerks about when the input has been held long enough.

Nearly every mission has either a trailing component where you watch an NPC stand at a console until the bar is full, you killing enormous waves of brain dead enemies until the bar runs out, or will throw a stupid timer which makes a boring fetch quest into a fury-inducing frustration festival where you just grapple through huge swarms of enemies because if you actually fight the enemies then you'll run out of time and fail the mission.

You'll get randomly annihilated by five attack choppers spawning instantly above you, having fighter jets kill every helicopter you touch within a minute of takeoff, or my favorite was a rally race down a mountain with checkpoints spaced out so poorly I had to backtrack each one and then the last point had an invisible wall which sent my shitty buggy into the water and failed the mission.

The enemies are useless, they'll shoot at you from six feet away and miss on foot, but will throw grenades perfectly from hundreds of feet away and will instantly see you pepper you with laser-perfect heavy weapons fire if they are in a vehicle, and as soon as Rico fires a weapon, literally dozens of troops and vehicles will spawn all around you, usually in a way that lets them crash into your car and send you off a cliff during the timed mission.

I left the game running overnight but I've got about 15 hours of real play time in, which has been a chore that I was enduring hoping that the game would get better, but it actually gets worse thanks to the ungodly heat levels, stupid allies who fail to do their parts of scripted missions leading to failures, random glitches and bugs, and a complete lack of compelling gameplay loop that made the prior games favorites of mine.

I got it on super sale at 95% off and I still think it was too much, I'm adding in some mods to let me burn through the game faster without all the horseshit, but it's only out of spite and not in the expectation that I'll actually have much fun doing so.

It's not bad, but its not great either. Coming off JC3 I was very disappointed with many of the changes they made here.

The BAD

1. No handheld explosives like in JC3 - instead you have to either engage with the new grapple systems or use the new alt fire modes found on most guns to get sort of real damage output against objects and vehicles.

2. the new grapple mechanics - imo the balloons are a gimmick which are good for a bit of messing around but not very helpful for actually clearing bases and the novelty wears off quckly. I miss the much stronger grapple from JC3 which could easily pull helicopters out of the sky. The default grapple here feels much weaker even when toggling it to its strongest pull.

3. enemies - once your alert meter goes up it can feel like a chore to get enemies off your back as they seem to pursue you for far longer and further than in JC3. they also seem to spawn more quickly as I rarely felt like I had actually cleared an area because new enemies would always pop up

4. activities - the flashy 5 star/gear system and reward screen in JC3 made every activity feel meaningful. In JC4 side activies like wingsuit courses feel hollow and not worth doing as there arent any great rewards and theres not even a screen popping up to say you did it in most cases.

5. bases - the goal is no longer about destroying red objects - you know, the straightforward objective of each base in JC3 that encouraged using the sandbox to wreak havoc? Red objects actually respawn now and the only point to destroying any of it is getting points towards the conquest mechanic which is token at best. This is already a huge disappointment but then each base now has an actual objective to do. This sounds cool on paper but the missions get recycled a lot and many of them now involve escorting NPCs or protecting an object - which I shouldn't have to explain is a very poor choice for a series about high mobility and explosions

6. vehicles - vehicles have ammo now which seems unnessecary. Some vehicles have enough ammo you'll never run out but others like the bomber jet seem to have enough for 1 or 2 runs before you may as well ditch the vehicle. Ground vehicles like tanks seem to be made out of paper now while air vehicles seem to be able to take more hits than in JC3 which is strange.

7. graphics - my PC is not very high spec anymore so take this with a grain of salt but I swear the graphics are worse here than in 3.

The GOOD

1. story - its hardly a work of art but the story is fine for the type of game this is. Its mostly held together by a few entertaining characters though Rico himself seems rather low energy for most of the game

2. story missions -credit where its due there are some cool moments here - the region finales involving the weather mechanics are the highlight with tornadoes, thunderstorms and sandstorms. Id even go so far as to say that the best missions here are a way bigger spectacle than any one mission in JC3.

3. map - personally I like Medici more but theres decent variety here with jungle, desert, and grassland regions

At the end of the day its a JC game and there is definitely some fun to be had here, especially if this is your first time with the series. For me though I felt that JC4 made unnecessary changes to the formula that took away what I liked so much about JC3, and it ends up being a very hollow experience where I finished the game and immediately went back to JC3 instead.

It's not a bad game, but it's not a good game either.

Vehicle controls are floaty and imprecise, especially aerial vehicles, since the dumbed down mouse movements for the helicopters cause oversteer, and planes are really stiff.

That brings me to the vehicle weaponry.
Most weapons seem identical across categories, for example, the cannons across all vehicles, be it light tank or artillery truck, feel identical, with a comically fast reload rate. It makes everything feel the same, especially when the life-span of vehicles are about 10 seconds, which is extremely frustrating.
You also have the issue of the third-person camera's aim being offset, so if you don't have the target in the crosshair, the round might just miss by a mile. This is especially noticeable with the Anti-Air vehicle, which doesn't seem to be specialised at all. Restrictive elevation on the guns, low fire-rate (the same cannons as the tanks I believe, but 2), and compounded by the aiming issue mentioned, hitting enemy jets is nigh impossible. Helicopters, sure, about as easy as with a normal tank.

Physics bugs in vehicles are common in my experience. I can drive the artillery truck, and shake violently for a second and lose half the vehicle's durability for no discernible reason. I can also try to take off with a helicopter and just combust, immediately dying. 

There's no localised damage on vehicles on a broader scale, so if your landing gear touches the ground a little hard your entire plane explodes, sending you to the shadow realm. In a game solely about chaos, you'd hope the aspects relating to chaotic environments would be polished.

Finishing off vehicles, their designs. They have slowly devolved to becoming more bland and futuristic. Many military vehicles are smooth kludges, with boring paint schemes (grey base and red stripes). Resistance vehicles on the other hand are on the opposite side of the spectrum, they're excessively garish. Green base with neon pinks, yellows and blues, no cool-factor, just a visual south-pole.

From vehicles to weapons, they are in a similar place to the vehicles'. 
Samey from gun to gun, with uninterestingly vague designs, and restrictive ammunition capacity for the amount of enemies you're going to undoubtedly face. 
Most weapons now have a secondary fire, which is nice, but sometimes very unfitting. The sniper rifle for example has a homing missile attached to the foregrip. That makes me sad. 
There are no pistols in this game, probably due to the fact that aiming is now optional. There's little point in shooting people, since a new group of 4 are going to show up in 2 seconds afterwards. Ideally you would find a tank and just shoot wherever until it catches fire 5 seconds later.

It just feels like gunplay has been demoted massively. Little to no reward for using them in anything but emergencies, similar guns apart from the extreme outliers, poor accuracy on automatic weapons, poor ammunition stocks, and overall to arcadey a feel to them.

Stationary guns are also frustrating. Very boring designs once again, indestructible, so if you have to stay around and area to do an objective, you bet your sweet gourd enemies will not leave it alone, ragdolling you every other breath while dealing with infinite helicopters, tanks and planes from the enemies. Restrictive fire-arcs once again, making them hard to use as the player.
And worst of all, "mortars", both as stationary weapons and on vehicles, are missile launchers. Homing missile launchers? How do you get it so wrong? It would be wonderful to have an indirect fire weapon, but it requires line of sight, and automatically locks on to whatever, so it's about as challenging to use as your lungs. 

Many weapon attacks are also choreographed, so you will see where an enemy helicopter is about to launch a missile. Is this a 3d bullet-hell game? What's the point, it's so stiff in practise. Besides, it doesn't really matter that they signal where they're shooting, because you will be hit by random explosions every 5th heartbeat anyway.


I think I've vented enough about that now, on to the player tools.
The parachute is as reliable as ever, no real complaints there.
The wingsuit is trickier to make a verdict on though. Out of every arcade-like aspect in the game, the wingsuit feel the least so. It is punishing with your airspeed, being sluggier than a snail to control when you're not at max speed. It's hard to describe, but turning feels like you're rotating inside a tincan inside a BINGO-tumbler. It's hard to be precise when you're rolling around like a marble. 
Grappling while wingsuiting is also a science, as quite often you will just reel into the ground, despite being parallel and trying to pitch up at the same time.

The grappling hook is very fancy, with a lot of toys and functions. It's excessive for me, because they're hard to use reliably in combat with the weird input delay sometimes, hangups, etc., but I appreciate that you have a lot of options. We like that.

There is sometimes noticable delay or lack of response when quickly switching from wingsuit or parachute to grappling for speed versus trying to stop wingsuiting/parachuting. Sometimes it just doesn't respond, and you reel straight into a wall while going mach, which ragdolls you, and probably sets you up to be rocketed/cannoned by the mosquito-like enemy presence.

Graphically the game looks nice, but it lacks vibrancy, and has what I can only describe as a brown filter over it.

The world feels pretty sparse despite being so big. I have a hard time finding unique details, since most towns seem to be the same church in the centre, and the same few houses scattered about. I'm probably generalising, but it's hard to look for details when there's no reason to visit the towns. There are no stores, very few interactions you can make with the surroundings there, no collectibles I've noticed, so I just fly over them. The few times I'm in towns, I'm probably crashing into the ground trying to do a wingsuit stunt, or picking up vehicle A to drive into checkpoint B (which are right next to each other)
With a map so large and towns so uninteresting, it kinda forces you to fly everywhere if you're not just in it for the chill vibes of a driving simulator. Most cars do feel like hotwheels though, being so zippy and slidey they're hard to control, but I guess there's a demographic for that.

Missed oppurtunity?
The ocean is vast, and lakes are plenty, but boats don't really serve a purpose when you have all the tools at your fingertips to completely ignore them. I really like boats, ships, barges and ferries, and their arsenals and functionality has only improved in this game, yet there's no real use for them?
I can get into a zippy speedboat to cross a lake, or I could fly along the coast in my wingsuit and get there before I find or deliver a boat.
I could stage a beach assault with a tank on a gorgeous landing craft, but I have to slowly get out of the landing craft as I beach it to jump into the tank, because It's singleplayer.

From map to map challenges. 
This is a really big problem for me, as there are hundreds, or what it feels like, thousands of micro challenges all over the map, which is what you have to complete to seemingly finish an area?
What are these challenges? 
Jump of a cliff/building/smokestack and fly through 3 checkpoints with your wingsuit.
Find a vehicle of a certain type and drive 15 meters to a checkpoint (they have static spawns of the exact vehicle you need very close to the goal)
And rarely, something that forces you to activate your single neuron. I had one challenge where I had to grapple an ATV up to closed off bridge. Kinda fun!
Another where I had to destroy some glass blocking my flight-path, also more fun!
But those are rare, and you seldom have to think at all to do theses supposed challenges, which makes them as menial as laundry, in a piece of interactive entertainment about chaos.

Is there some captured news reporter who is alerting the citizens of Solis of all the "approved changes DiRavello" is implementing after liberating each base? Of course not!

Instead of straight-forward liberation missions where you need to destroy all the assets in a particular base, it's converted to a rebel-led mission where key items needs to be activated (activate all the switches in a given area, transport an operative to a destination point and wait until he "hacks" the system), which sound like it would be good, but honestly, drags the game longer than needs to be. Rico's personality has been neutered greatly. Where he was lovingly cocky and self-assured before, he's now reduced to being surprised he was able to accomplish whatever task he was setting out to do.

*Some JC3 to JC4 comparison talk
Get it on sale. Otherwise, no.

Pros

-If you mess around with the settings, you can get some rather beautiful landscapes. The draw distance for foliage and such is not great, no better than JC3 I guess, but this doesn't really kill the pretty views. It's a different lighting compared to JC3, not as much glow and maybe more shadows but certainly beautiful in their own rights. The lighting change between regions can be off putting but it's quick so eh.

-Some abilities from JC3 are just standard in this one (no more having to do challenges to unlock abilities). 

-The map is massive (the rivers are small). It's a large map with a lot of verticality and areas with updrafts near cliffs (not a lot though).

-The tethers easily make this game. 3 different tether load-outs each able to customized (activate via tap/hold/automatic), 3 different tether types (balloons, tether, and boosters). Each have mods and can be used in clever ways, balloons to make cover from aerial attacks or to just fly away those threats, the boosters can just launch people away BUT they can overclock to be used kind of like in JC3, and the tethers....well, they can do a power yank otherwise the same. I've had a blast realizing I can attach boosters in the right spots on the mech to fly around with it with perfect control, mild control with a flying limo.

-The freedom of movement. I have been enjoying this game mainly for this fact. I got the DLC, get when on sale, and even without the jet boost and the hoverboard it's still crazy fun. The tether to pull yourself around in the wingsuit is as satisfying as ever.


Mixed:

Challenges Gone:
-Challenges are pretty much gone. Replaced with "pass through x going x kph", "pass through x in x", "wingsuit through 3 rings in x time", and maybe something else as dull. They're easier to do which is nice and do enough of a type and you can unlock tether mods or wingsuit mods. I think some other stuff but nothing I can remember right now. So if you liked challenges, sorry. 


Wingsuit:
-The wingsuit has been reworked so it feels less "flighty". Because when flying with a wingsuit, one doesn't want to be weightless like a bird in JC3 but as a real Rico. 
-If you get the DLC to have the jet wingsuit f you will be sad to know that you cannot take off from land or sea and the minigun is gone replaced with missiles instead. NOTE: If you have all DLC you can just use the hoverboard to surface fast and then wingsuit when jumping, you will get a good amount of air.
-Airbraking looks and handles awful, if you stall too long you just cancel out of the wingsuit. It just felt more sensible in JC3
-The missiles you get are not lock-on and do not even go where you exactly aimed, it's an area attack with 4 missiles with decent aoe. The problem is attacking air targets or anything not exactly near a large flat plane making you have to get pretty close to hit with a missile or to kind of cheese the aim to get one missile to hit where you want.

-Destruction is mixed. But I think it's because the physics are just wonky, you'll notice it a lot with tether+reeling things. Not everything breaks in a way that looks right, a feather light giant satellite dish for instance...

Cons:

-The game is jank. I had to reverify my files, a common need, because my DLC didn't appear in the black market drops. Thankfully, only had to do this once.

-No pistols. Stuck with 2 weapons. Resupply!

-The map is massive, but it's still barren. The devs get how to do landscapes, but cities they just cannot seem to understand that they need more. Solis is 80% barren and 100% black hand everywhere. The game is kind of a good example of getting the big picture but not all the small details *map still pretty.

-No distance is reflected when setting a waypoint or tracking an objective. Just kills the scale.

-No running.

-The "cutscenes" are just awful. I've messed around with my settings but I just cannot fix the sharp light, lip sync issues, and character faces looking awful. They don't look bad in game, even though the cutscenes are in-game (maybe that's why?). They are just poorly optimized

-Tom Sheldon is not Tom Sheldon, the character looks nothing like him.

-The tethers (yea they suck too). The game's combat really wants you to go fast and move. So when trying to make quick tethers to boost helis/tanks into the atmosphere (because I have no explosives), sometimes the tethers just don't deploy fluidly, I have to hold to deploy and let go to deploy the end of the tether, same as 3, yet it gets buggy. I'll try to do it and Rico just doesn't shoot the end of the tether so I have to press the button again and it just cancels the tether out. Sometimes I'll try and I'll reel myself into certain death. It's just as if the game cannot handle wanting to shoot 10 tethers in succession.

-Chaos is meaningless (from how it was). Chaos can be gained from pretty much anything, and in fact, you get it more from doing ANYTHING other than blowing up enemy structures. There's no sense of accomplishment from destroying bases as things will just repopulate (kind of like when you beat JC3 and you can select to do that but you don't get to choose). 

-So little to blow up, no grenades or c4 to even do it with. They're just gone, enemies have grenades but you don't. The lack of this forces one of your weapons to always be an rpg or another reliable explosive. Or using tether mods for balloons and boosters to handle them. While you never need to blow up anything big anymore (sad) I'd think you'd still want some explosives to help with that tank or helicopter making you hate life.

-The water near or inside Solis looks so awful. Waterfalls look anti-climatic, calm river just goes into a gushing waterfall, they all do this. The mixed to this is the water outside is really nice. So I am not sure how much of this was deliberate but couldn't be realized how they wanted perhaps.

-Wanted Forever. If you get on alert, honestly, just call a pilot and fast travel to the same spot, it cancels the alert lazily... Can't really escape by air because the helis go the speed of jets and the jets are already shooting at you, go on the ground? They will hunt you down hard. I will go into the mountains and just as they call off the the search there's always a heli just a moment away from actually spotting me. It makes doing some things just a pain.

The enemies, so many enemies and they all know exactly where you are. And they all have grenades and decent aim and blend into the environment because the devs didn't give them a highlight or outline silhouette to help you distinguish them beyond their muzzle flash or all the red and green dots aimed at you. It gets worse when you have to stand in a small area to complete an objective and the enemies just keep coming and building up

-Resupply is tedious beyond all reason. Do you need to resupply your 2 guns and get a vehicle to bail out? Easy, call in 3 separate pilots and wait for 3 drops one by one to do so :) 

Rebel Drops / Pilots: (Kind of sucks)
-Rebel drop and fast travel beacons have been reworked into Pilots. Pilots can call down ONE thing or fast travel you to a location. Afterwards it's a several minute cooldown to use them again. You can have a good amount of pilots, so no more having to get more beacons, yay. BUT pilots can only call down one item at a time AND pilots wait for each pilot to drop off their supply one by one. I haven't timed it but, opening comms link, going to resupply, opening their options, selecting the option, selecting to call it in, selecting where I want to call it in, waiting 7 or so seconds to fall (+ however longer until it is settled on the ground), then grabbing it. Only to wait 7 or more seconds again to get my next resupply drop or my getaway vehicle. You can sit in the comms and this does speed the timer for the resupply and pilot but...why not make it that fast always?

[h1]Just Cause 4...A perfect example of the saying "If it's not broken, don't fix it"[/h1]

I've not reviewed a game in years, but I felt a certain need to address this instalment of Just Cause in particular. Before anything I would like to mention that on sale, this game is a steal for £2.39 and would advise trying it if you have not picked it up yet, but other than that id advise to save your money and get Just Cause 3 instead, as it has arguably set the standard for how entertaining a Just Cause game can be.

Starting off with some positives, the selection of vehicles in my eyes are great and they are never too hard to find, although their limited ammo defeats the purpose of causing unrealistic levels of destruction (which makes Just Cause satisfying in the first place), you can never go wrong with leaving a base and simply calling in another bomber as your supply drops only have a 5 minute cooldown timer. The environment, like the previous instalments is vibrant, and natural tornados alongside it definitely adds to the immersion.

Cons:
The base takeovers are linear and very repetitive, consisting of either hacking 4 terminals or destroying 4 generators, waiting at a console for a few minutes while waves of NPCs try their hardest to kill you,after which you immedietly take over said base without braking a sweat, making destroying gas and fuel tanks and other infrastructure completely pointless. They've essentially managed to make a game about destruction with barely any incentive to destroy anything.

Your allies in this story are robotic, have zero personality and are very forgettable, as for the villains, you have a megalomanic owner of a private military group and their commander who by the end of the game you question why they needed to be taken out. Meanwhile Just Cause 2 had a midget (probably based off Sukharto's rule of Indonesia) hellbent on launching nukes after cutting ties with the agency, and Just Cause 3 being a personal story for Rico as Di Ravello (an Italian version of Lukashenko?) helped make Rico an orphan and was sitting on a rare earth element that could be weaponised made completing the story at least satisfying. (spoiler warning?) [spoiler]After overthrowing the villain who is our ally (like Di Ravello USED to be) for what seems like no reason...ONLY THEN does Rico realise that MAYBE he's being used as a pawn by the agency, its a plot hole that exists when it doesn't need to. Especially after "trusting" Sheldon again for the third time now.[/spoiler]

The unlockable gimmick weapons (literally just a boat and a truck) are boring and you'll only ever use them once, I think many would agree that a Bavarium rocket launcher is much more universal and fun to use.

In terms of looking at the future, I think a Just Cause 5 game should bring back the factions and criminal organisations that Just Cause 2 had, an often overlooked detail like this which I think can drastically increase mission variety and immersion, in addition, Just Cause 4's frontline system I think should stay according to borders of captured land (as well as the fact it represents that there is in fact, a civil war going on) but not have it an integral to capturing additional land as i'd much rather prefer the satisfying activity of destroying bases with the myriad of new vehicles and weapons in this game.

In conclusion, I will give Just Cause 4 a verdict of a 5.7/10, astronomically mid. Unless it's on a sale I cant recommend this game to anyone.

I'll start with what this game does well: I picked this up at like 90% sale, and ever since then I've been playing this on and off, on "autopilot" if you will, not really thinking. It's a fun game to boot up just to destroy stuff and watch explosions, and all the different vehicles and weapons combinations can turn out to be extremely fun.

Now, for the bad: this game fundamentally fails to be what it wants to be.
The story is boring and unrelatable, and the whole feel of the game just feels like a JC3 clone instead of a sequel. It's trying to imitate JC3's success, but it just can't.
Rico, the MAIN CHARACTER, is built horribly for the difficulty of the game - the developers made him very overpowered in terms of offense, with his impressive arsenal, but on the defensive side he lacks horribly, and can almost be considered a "glass cannon", very powerful yet very weak. So much so that even hitting a surface while while gliding can kill you. You'll find yourself dying frequently to enemies since they are PACKED with weapons.
There is no way to change this either as the game progresses, as in to reward completion - nah, you're just a puny WMD who can be downed with just 2-3 grenades. No skill points, no leveling, no nothing.

Other than that, missions are extremely boring and repetitive, and most of the time unrewarding. You get a couple hundred XP points to sub-types of the reel. It's not even that bad if you're playing this game casually like I am, but for certain missions, some of which are even part of a mini-campaign, [spoiler] like Garland's Motion Picture missions - which in the last one where you complete it and supposedly go to the premiere of the movie, instead of actually showing a short cutscene or something, you literally get a black-screen and get told "thanks". [/spoiler] you feel like you just wasted 10 minutes so a random civilian can tell you "Thanks" in the generic civilian voice - no reward, nothing.
Certain missions also require you to protect an NPC or a vehicle/machine - which just like protecting yourself can be a massively exhausting chore. The checkpoints are terrible too, so if you fail just before the end you gotta do it all over again.

This is a great game if you love playing games casually and mindlessly. I would still recommend to buy it only on at least 50% off sale.

Just Cause 4 should have been the sandbox to end all sandboxes. The franchise itself represented a departure from the usual rules of the open world sandbox by allowing the players un-parallelled mobility, and Just Cause 3 took this player mobility to it's logical conclusion as well as abandoning any pretense of trying to gate keep the player's power level behind contrived obstacles.

Just Cause 4 was a day one purchase for me. I was a huge fan of the franchise when it existed, and within an hour of firing it up I had already rage quit and didn't touch it again for 6 years. 

Where did it all go wrong? There's a whole story here about the closure of Avalanche New York, private investment, tax policy, greed, and art for profit's sake, but rather than marinating on the game we should have played, lets talk about the one we got:

Solis is beautiful, but dead compared to JC3s Medici and especially JC2's Panay... there is actually quite a lot of character to the world and some incredible location design... but the game only bothers to engage you with it once. The story missions, strikes, etc never start to feel like an organic part of the world around you. Just Cause 4's challenges never rise above the level of menial nonsense. Everything just feels like it was pasted into the world. Did you find a light house? You bet your sweet bippy there's gonna a wing suit challenge where you have to flop lazily to the ground through the exact same three rings as the other twenty lighthouses pasted along the shore. There's something to the order of 300 such challenges the game asks you to complete, but if I had to guess I would say there are actually fewer  than 30 unique challenges and the rest is just "That other challenge, but over here now."

A not-insignificant portion of the game just... literally does not work. Stunt ramps are placed against oncoming traffic, which in itself would not be a problem except for the algorithm the game uses to populate the world around you. The game will ALWAYS draw a car at a position relative to your location to keep the world busy. In the event of oncoming traffic, this system then works with the NPCs self-preservation, to guarantee that on five out of five approaches to a poorly placed ramp, an NPC in the oncoming traffic lane will ALWAYS stop between the player and the ramp. 

So you start problem solving. Maybe if you block traffic, you think, that will solve the problem. But it never does. Now imagine spending multiple minutes/attempts/deaths trying to get just ONE of what should be some of the easiest stunts in the game, and when you finally manage to set it up so that you can actually hit the ramp, it dead-stops your vehicle killing you instantly because the stunt ramp was never set up at an appropriate level to the ground in the first place or the developers just never bothered to check if the vehicle they assigned to that challenge had the wheel clearance to actually use the ramp they placed. 

At the highest level, you really only have two or three attempts at any given task before the background noise of freedom fighters, Blackhand soldiers, panicked bystanders, and exploding combinations of all three makes success, if not survival, an impossibility. A cascade of small annoyances quickly gather strength into an Avalanche of bullshit. The faster you learn to never trust the developers or their intended solutions to any of the missions or puzzles in the game, the happier you are bound to be. 

Every Strike mission in the game relies on an infinite supply of enemies to make the challenge. Most of the times this doesn't make much of a difference... but on a few select missions the game decides to add another infinite supply of enemies which quickly breaks the game. 

Sargento's storyline culminates in a mission called Beachhead that mandates you be pursued by two gunship helicopters at all times. It also mandates that you sink several large warships. The type of ammunition that you need to handle both of these tasks is finite, and if you're at all clever you quickly see where that mission becomes a seriously un-fun slog. Even if you luck out and are able to tether the two gunships together before they can start making your life difficult, two more instantly spawn. I don't mean, "two more will eventually show up." I mean, two new helicopters will INSTANTLY spawn behind you. They will already be targeting you before the last two chassis hit the ground.

Negotiating enemy escalation with the AI in this game honestly feels like arguing with someone who is too committed to admit they were wrong. On a fairly regular basis, the game will just forget that the enemy is supposed to stop looking for you after a while. Like when you're grappled to the top of a cave, in the middle of nowhere, with no enemy soldiers around for kilometers. 

Like before, this would just be a minor annoyance by itself... by the time you have boosters and air lifters dealing with most enemy units is facile. But after a long enough time being hunted, the game seems to decide that the only way to deescalate is to just kill you outright. Enemy air units will literally start to kamikaze you with a predictability that would make Darth Bob blush. The combination of these two factors does occasionally result in hilarity, like when you spend ten minutes grappled to the ceiling of said cave just to listen to the game endlessly call in air support only for the Blackhand jets to explode trying to fly through the mountain to reach you.

If you're a huge fan of capture & control game play and sandbox games, you can probably squeeze enough blood out of this stone to make it worth a deeply discounted purchase. However, if you're a die-hard fan of the franchise who just finished 3 and is hoping for the next big blow-out... keep looking.

Just Cause 4, the latest addition to the Just Cause franchise, fails to impress with its lack of innovation and identical gameplay to its predecessor, Just Cause 3. Despite being marketed as a brand new game, Just Cause 4 feels like nothing more than a cheap knock-off of the previous game, with only a handful of improvements that do little to justify its existence as a separate title.

The improvements in Just Cause 4, such as the inclusion of extreme weather conditions and new gadgets, do little to add to the overall experience. The weather effects are nothing more than a novelty, and the gadgets are more of the same old tools that players have been using in the previous games with little additions. The lack of any significant improvements or innovations leaves players wondering why they should even bother with this game when they could just stick to playing Just Cause 3.

In conclusion, Just Cause 4 is a lackluster addition to the Just Cause franchise that fails to live up to the expectations set by its predecessor. The game feels like a cash grab, with minimal changes to the gameplay and a lack of any meaningful improvements. Save your money and stick to Just Cause 3 if you're looking for a fun and engaging open-world experience.
